item.title: Referees will be short-staffed at least one NFL game after nationwide ground stop
item.description: Aug 20, 2026; Inglewood, California, USA; The NFL shield logo on the field at SoFi Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images Friday’s nationwide ground stop wreaked havoc on air travel across the country, and the NFL is feeling the effects heading into Week 10. The league has been forced to shuffle its officiating crews for Sunday’s games. One game will be a little more shorthanded than the rest. The Carolina Panthers and New Orleans Saints will play without a replay official in the stadium, with those duties being handled from New York instead. Nationwide Ground Stop The FAA issued a nationwide ground stop at 3:54 p.m. ET on Friday, and airspace didn’t reopen until 8:15 p.m. ET. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said the stop was caused by switches and routers becoming overloaded and going down. More than 4,700 flights were canceled on Friday, with about 700 more already canceled for Saturday. Duffy also warned that it would “take us some time to get back to capacity.” As a result, the NFL adjusted its officiating assignments so that officials would be working games within driving distance of their hometowns. That means three backup referees will be calling games on Sunday, according to Tom Pelissero of The Ringer and Netflix. Umpire Duane Heydt will referee Panthers-Saints, while umpire Barry Anderson will work Jaguars-Titans and side judge Don Willard will referee both Dolphins-Colts and Steelers-Bengals. No Replay Official for Panthers-Saints On Saturday, Pelissero reported one more change for the Panthers-Saints game. “One more officiating change for Sunday: The Saints-Panthers game won’t have a replay official in the stadium, so his duties will instead be handled by the replay center in New York, per sources,” Pelissero wrote on X . That could put a strain on the league office, especially since Panthers-Saints is one of seven games in the 1 p.m. ET window, Pro Football Talk noted. Between a backup referee and no replay official in the building, the Panthers and Saints will be playing under some unusual circumstances. Needless to say, fans will be watching the officiating closely. The post Referees will be short-staffed at least one NFL game after nationwide ground stop appeared first on The Comeback: Today’s Top Sports Stories & Reactions .

item.title: Kentucky Wildcats in the college football rankings roundup and Sunday news
item.description: Last night was a disappointing loss for the Kentucky Wildcats. There’s no way around it. Things started off promising for Kentucky, as they scored on their opening drive on a 15-play, 86-yard drive that lasted more than 8 minutes. However, Kentucky’s offense struggled the remainder of the game, as the Cats would only manage 156 yards of offense the rest of the night. The defense was strong in the first half, forcing the Gators to punt on all five of their offensive possessions in the first half, as the Gators only managed to score via a safety on a controversial holding call against the Wildcats that the officials said occurred in the end zone. The second half was a different story, though, as Kentucky simply could not stop Florida QB Aaron Philo from consistently picking up yards on the ground. Philo, who entered last night’s game with 104 rushing yards on 44 carries this season, finished with 102 yards on 15 carries against Kentucky, nearly all of which came in the second half. The loss essentially knocks Kentucky out of playoff contention, as the Cats fall to 7-3 on the season. Kentucky entered last night’s game ranked 11th in the College Football Playoff rankings, and 13th in the AP Poll and Coaches Poll. After a second consecutive loss, where will Kentucky land in the new rankings? Chip Patterson from CBS Sports projects Kentucky will be ranked 17th. Thomas Goldkamp from On3 projects Kentucky to fall to #20. Matthew Glenesk from USA Today projects Kentucky to fall to #15 in the CFP rankings. As a reminder, the AP will not release their top 25 rankings today as they normally would due to the Oklahoma-Ole Miss game being postponed. The AP will release their rankings tomorrow. Where do you think Kentucky will land in the new rankings? Tweet of the Day Check on your Kentucky sports fan friends. Nightmare week for the Cats. — Kyle Tucker (@KyleTuckerCBB) November 15, 2026 We’ve been through it the last week. Headlines Florida dominated Kentucky at the line of scrimmage – KSR The Cats have to be better in the trenches. What’s next for UK Sports after awful week? – Cats Pause We need some good news. UK WBB hosts Eastern Michigan today – UK Athletics Go Cats! Kentucky State falls in conference title game after time management meltdown – Yahoo Brutal… Week 11 winners and losers – SI Georgia continues to look really good. Louisville-UNC game ends in a brawl – Yahoo That could’ve went a lot worse. Oklahoma AD rips Ole Miss, SEC for Sunday game – ESPN Honestly, he has a point. Clemson and Dabo continue to spiral – CBS Sports Things are not going well at Clemson. Jeremiah Smith breaks Big 10 receiving yards record – ESPN Another notable accomplishment for the Heisman contender. NFL could look at onside kick rules – Bleacher Report Onside kick recoveries have nearly become extinct. Georgia football commit passes away following medical emergency – Yahoo Just awful…

item.title: Wilson’s Bold Start Lifts No. 9 Indiana Past USC In Key Win
item.description: Credit: Robert Goddin-Imagn Images No. 9 Indiana needed a spark to fix its postseason resume, and fill-in quarterback Grant Wilson delivered it in a 27-13 victory over No. 18 USC. The Hoosiers had struggled to score points or move the ball since late October, but the team looked like a complete unit on Saturday night. After taking over for the injured Josh Hoover, seventh-year player Wilson, who had not started since 2024, immediately pushed the offense to be more aggressive. Coach Curt Cignetti made the call to start Wilson on his way home from the Oct. 31 road trip against Minnesota. “He pulled me to the side while out there at practice, and he goes, ‘You’re going to go with the ones,’ and then turned around and walked away,” Wilson said of the moment he learned he was the starter per ESPN . The offense threw deep right from the opening drive. Abandoning the Safe Plan Indiana had been playing too conservatively for the last two weeks, a style that Cignetti admitted the team hated. “We’ve been kind of playing in the tent, so to speak, the last two weeks, conservative,” Cignetti said. The team immediately looked downfield, with Wilson’s first completion going for 47 yards to Shazz Preston. “We took some shots there on the first drive, kind of set the tone for the game, got them to back up a little bit, play their shell, and then we got them to switch out of it,” said Wilson per ESPN. Nine of his 17 completions gained at least 12 yards, showing that the offense was willing to take risks to win. A Boost for the Whole Team Wilson finished with 305 passing yards, two touchdowns, and one interception, leading the Hoosiers to their best win of the season. The passing game gave the offensive line a break from constant run-blocking duties, which helped the entire unit play with more confidence. Khobie Martin also helped the ground game after missing the first half of the season with an injury. Despite the win, Cignetti did not promise that Wilson would keep the starting job. “What he’s been going through is tough,” Wilson said about Hoover. “I don’t wish that on anyone. … He’s gone through so much with his shoulder. He’s a great teammate.”

item.title: Banton pushes case and bowlers sparkle for inconsistent England
item.description: Baker was making his first appearance against Australia [Getty Images] Second one-day international, Adelaide England 355-6 (50 overs): Banton 121, Cox 67, Root 62 Australia 220 all out (44.3 overs): Green 64, Renshaw 63; Atkinson 4-28 England won by 135 runs; series level at 1-1 Scorecard Tom Banton scored a century and Sonny Baker and Gus Atkinson impressed with the ball as England's wildly inconsistent one-day team hammered Australia to set up a series decider. Banton scored a fine 121 – pushing his case for selection further with a second ODI hundred – in England's 355-6. After being knocked over for 131 two days ago in Perth, England's total was their highest in one-day internationals in Australia. And then their bowlers, who failed to defend 430 against Sri Lanka last month and were undone by an improbable last-wicket partnership against Pakistan, reduced Australia to 29-4 inside seven overs and easily closed out a 135-run victory. The win ends a seven-match losing run against Australia across formats in Adelaide - and a run of six consecutive defeats by Australia in 50-over cricket away from home. But, more significantly, it corrects their course after those damaging defeats against Sri Lanka, Pakistan and Australia and offers positives amid the frustrations going into the decider on Wednesday (03:30 GMT) in Hobart. Baker a smart selection Will the real England please stand up? Before those defeats in Rawalpindi, Lahore and Perth, England had won three ODI series this year. This win only adds to the feeling they are extremely difficult to figure out. Banton was superb and, even more encouragingly, Atkinson and Baker were too. This England team has often struggled for new-ball wickets and Baker, brought in for Jamie Overton in an attempt to correct that fault, found significant swing. He took the key wicket of Australia captain Mitchell Marsh, taken high at slip by a diving Joe Root, for two. Atkinson used nip to nick off Travis Head for seven – the second match in a row he has dismissed the Australia left-hander – and also have both Cooper Connolly and Josh Inglis caught behind. Career-best figures of 4-28 are reward for good recent performance that have often gone unrewarded. England were not perfect. They dropped four catches – first Inglis and then Matt Renshaw and Cameron Green, who made 63 and 64 respectively to drag out Australia's score. But by the end, Sam Curran had taken two wickets in two balls, including bowling Jack Edwards with his moon ball, in a boost after his poor run. Green was also out stumped when the ball deflected off Jordan Cox's shin and onto the stumps and Liam Dawson took 2-41 as he was preferred again to Adil Rashid. These are the performances that suggest England can challenge at next year's World Cup, but plenty more are needed. Banton pushes case Banton's chance as opener has come courtesy of Jacob Bethell's knee injury. In nine innings, he has scored four fifties and two hundreds. The spot should now be his

item.title: Wenger decides not to challenge Fifa chief Infantino
item.description: Arsene Wenger had considered running for the Fifa presidency [Getty Images] Former Arsenal manager Arsene Wenger has decided not to stand against Gianni Infantino as a candidate in Fifa's presidential election. The Frenchman had been considering running for the job but sources have told BBC Sport that he has ruled himself out. Current world football chief Infantino's position was plunged into crisis by a backlash caused by his failed plan to sell commercial stakes in the World Cup to private investors. Wenger - who is Fifa's head of global development - would have had the backing of European football's governing body Uefa, which has spearheaded opposition to Infantino. On Saturday, French newspaper L'Equipe reported that Wenger was unlikely to challenge his boss. Wenger has credibility throughout the footballing world, and this will be a significant boost to Infantino as he seeks a fourth term as president. Uefa is said to still be hopeful of finding an alternative candidate before Wednesday's deadline. One influential figure in the group of stakeholders opposed to Infantino told BBC Sport the news was "a real shame". "Even if not perfect, I do think he could have galvanized many around the world," they added. Former Tottenham defender Ramon Vega was the first person to put his name forward in October. Japan Football Association honorary president Kozo Tashima has also announced his intention to stand. However, sources have told BBC Sport that the 68-year-old has not yet secured the necessary five endorsements from member associations ahead of Wednesday's deadline but is "still fighting hard". Amid the fallout over FFE, Wenger, who has traditionally been loyal to Infantino, distanced himself from the aborted plot. "I was not involved in this strategic plan and first became aware of the project through media reports," Wenger said at the time. "The decision to withdraw the project was absolutely necessary and beyond question, because I firmly believe in an independent Fifa that serves our game with commitment, transparency and integrity." Infantino has retained support in South America, Africa and Asia, and recently insisted he has the backing of the "vast, vast majority" of world football. FIFA has been approached for comment. item.title: Arsenal star plays through illness for national team
item.description: Arsenal star plays through illness for national team Martin Odegaard was up all night feeling unwell before Norway’s match against Wales on Saturday, but he went on to play 90 minutes anyway. Photo by Michael Steele/Getty Images Norway captain Martin Odegaard hasn’t missed a minute of his country’s 2026/27 Nations League campaign so far, but there was a strong argument for him sitting out of Saturday’s game against Wales . According to Norway manager Stale Solbakken , Odegaard was up all night before the game due to illness, but he pushed to play 90 minutes anyway. “We have had a captain who has been lying around all night vomiting,” Solbakken said . “All credit to him for going the distance. We had a conversation during the break that he should just go for it from the start and let us know when the tank was empty.” Photo by Michael Steele/Getty Images Odegaard’s Norway teammate Patrick Berg confirmed his manager’s claims, praising the player for being able to finish the match anyway. “I understood that Martin had a bad night,” Berg said. “It’s not exactly optimal when you’re going out and playing a football game. It’s strong of him to be able to finish. “As far as I know, the illness is only affecting one person. We can only hope that it stays that way. But it is not unusual for it to spread.” Photo by Marius Nordnes / Nordnes Foto/Getty Images For what it’s worth, the game went well. Odegaard created three chances as Norway won 3-1, ending a run of three consecutive defeats. Norway had been slipping towards relegation, but they’re now safe from automatic relegation, and they could even achieve a top-two finish and make the Nations League quarter-finals if they win their final game against Denmark . If they don’t win that match, they’ll be playing in the relegation play-offs in March. Photo by Marius Nordnes / Nordnes Foto/Getty Images

item.title: Jason Kelce reveals what he hates about Eagles that could make owner Jeffrey Lurie angry
item.description: Photo by Terence Lewis/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Jason Kelce has a take that could make Philadelphia Eagles owner Jeffrey Lurie angry. Jason Kelce spent his entire 13-year NFL career with the Philadelphia Eagles and retired as a franchise legend in 2024. Even though Kelce is no longer an active player, he always shows unwavering support for the Eagles through his ‘New Heights’ podcast. Speaking on his podcast, Kelce recently revealed what he hates about the Eagles that won’t sit well with owner Jeffrey Lurie. Jason Kelce wants Philadelphia Eagles to wear retro jerseys Kelce explained that he’s stunned that teams no longer prefer wearing retro jerseys. For the Eagles in particular, he shared his favourite retro jerseys that predate the time that Lurie has owned the franchise. “I don’t know why everybody is not wearing retro jerseys. I hate all of the new jerseys. … Kelly Green, in my opinion, should be the main jersey for the Eagles. “Technically, Midnight Green was instituted in the 90s when Jeffrey Lurie bought the team. Jeffrey would not be happy that I’m saying this, but I do like the Kelly Green more,” Kelce said. He added, “Midnight Green was better when it was Reebok-owned. There was a sheen and a shininess to it. Now that the Nike jerseys are stretchy and it’s not the same material, the Midnight Green doesn’t look anywhere near as cool.” For context, Lurie bought the Eagles in 1994, and it didn’t take long for him to end the Kelly Green jerseys, as the Midnight Green jerseys were introduced in 1996. While the Eagles have been successful in the Midnight Green jerseys, Kelce still thinks the Kelly Green ones were superior. item.title: Erling Haaland snaps back at questions over Man City charges
item.description: Erling Haaland says he is "incredibly happy" at Manchester City , insisting his focus remains on performing rather than potential sanctions against the club . City have launched an appeal having been found guilty of more than 100 breaches of the Premier League ’s financial regulations. If the verdict stands, the club could be subjected to heavy sanctions, including huge points deductions or demotion. Haaland addressed the case following Norway’s 3-1 Nations League win over Wales in Oslo on Saturday night, where he registered his 66th goal in 60 international appearances. “This is a question I struggle to answer, because it’s a legal battle between the Premier League and Manchester City,” Haaland told Norwegian broadcaster TV2. “Am I supposed to answer that? I don’t really know. It’s a difficult question to answer when I don’t know that much about it. “To be completely honest, I’m focused on trying to perform for Manchester City. A club I signed a five-year deal with in 2022, and a new nine-and-a-half-year deal in late 2024. “I think that says everything about the matter. I’m a City player and I’m incredibly happy there.” Asked if the situation affects his City future, Haaland replied: “I understand that you want a little headline here, but as I said I signed a long-term contract in 2024. Erling Haaland says he is happy and focused on performing amid the Premier League club’s off-field issues (PA Wire) “I’d say I made a pretty good choice by joining City in 2022. We can all agree on that. “I won’t say it myself, but look at the trophies I’ve won and how I’ve developed on and off the pitch. “I’m standing here after winning an international 3-1. Things aren’t going so well in the Premier League, but we’ll try to turn that around against Fulham (on Saturday).” City maintain they have a “comprehensive body of irrefutable evidence” to support their case, despite being found guilty by an independent commission in September. The commission’s damning findings included breaches relating to the concealment of funding worth more than £830million over a nine-year period between 2009 and 2018. Haaland was asked about the case after Norway’s 3-1 Nations League victory over Wales, in which he scored his 66th goal in 60 international appearances (AP) Haaland said the period under investigation happened before he joined City, and in the interview he painstakingly pointed out each stage of his football journey during that time. He also name checked fellow Norwegian players Abdisalam Ibrahim, Martin Samuelsen, Omar Elabdellaoui and Kjetil Haug, who spent time at City during that era. Haaland said: “The investigation covered 2009-2018. I assume the answers will come. “I don’t know when. I haven’t read much about it.”

item.title: NCAAW gameday discussion: Will No. 3 USC’s JuJu Watkins add a win over No. 1 South Carolina to her illustrious resume?
item.description: JuJu Watkins. | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images There’s a reason that whichever team wins tonight’s 2027 WNBA Draft Lottery is almost guaranteed to select JuJu Watkins with the No. 1 overall pick in April’s draft Robbed of her junior season due to ACL recovery, Watkins still has compiled one of the more complete resumes in women’s college basketball history. As a freshman, Watkins powered USC back to relevance, taking the Trojans from a No. 21 preseason ranking up to as high as No. 3 in the AP poll and all the way to the Elite Eight. Along the way, she starred with 30 or more points in 14 games, apexing with a 51-point masterpiece against No. 4-ranked Stanford. She also helped the Trojans take down the Cardinal in the final(ish) Pac-12 Tournament title game, and that was after putting 33 points on cross-town rival UCLA in the semis to help elevate USC to the tourney trophy for the first time in a decade. JuJu Watkins vs. #4 Stanford 😳 ▪️51 PTS ▪️11 REB ▪️2 AST ▪️4 STL ▪️14-26 FG (53%) ▪️6-11 3PT (54%) ▪️17-19 FT ▪️W USC : 67 Stanford: 58 #NCAAWBB | 📸 @USCWBB pic.twitter.com/SGo07TOM7Q — The Committee Sports Group (@TheCommitteeSG) February 3, 2024 Finishing with a season-long scoring average of 27.1 points per game, along with 7.3 boards, 3.3 assists, 2.3 steals and 1.6 blocks per contest, JuJu swept any and all freshman of the year honors, in addition to earning All-America selections. With expectations raised for her sophomore campaign, Watkins proved perfectly comfortable performing in the spotlight. She again made 30-plus-point performances seem routine, with seven games scoring 30 or more. Watkins avenged the Trojans’ Elite Eight loss to UConn, invading Storrs and escaping with a two-point win. She also notched another signature win, leading USC over then-No. 1 UCLA in the Galen Center before then beating the Bruins in Pauley Pavilion in the second regular-season matchup between the two LA rivals. JUJU WATKINS IN THE WIN VS PREVIOUSLY UNDEFEATED #1 RANKED UCLA 38 POINTS 11 REBOUNDS 5 ASSISTS 8 BLOCKS (CAREER HIGH) 6-9 3 FG USC WINS 71-60 #FIGHTON ✌️❤️ pic.twitter.com/vKcc3hvgks — Watkins Report (@JWatkinsReport) February 14, 2025 The accolades thus accumulated, as almost every major individual honor belonged to Watkins after she averaged almost 24 points, 6.8 rebounds, 3.4 assists. 2.2 steals and 1.8 blocks per game, all with improved scoring efficiency. Only the aforementioned ACL injury could halt her ascendence into an all-time stratosphere, cutting short her second NCAA Tournament and sidelining her from the sport for over a year. A national championship, of course, is the missing piece from Watkins’ resume, as Edwin Garcia just emphasized . That accomplishment would take her from an all-timer to a near-immortal. One other achievement is also absent. A win over South Carolina. item.title: ‘Loserdom’ – U.S. soccer legends ripped for calling Pep Guardiola a bad fit to lead the USMNT
item.description: Photo by FRANCK FIFE/AFP via Getty Images The recent reports linking the United States Men’s National Team to Pep Guardiola as Mauricio Pochettino’s replacement as manager have irked two former USMNT stars. The United States have always been considered one of the sleeping giants in world soccer, as the sport has not had the cultural appeal of American football (NFL), basketball, or baseball. But success at the international level could change that for the next generation. As USMNT have recently committed to building themselves up as an international powerhouse in the sport, they’re linked with a big-money move to make Guardiola their new manager. However, it seems two recent legends heavily disagree. Landon Donovan and Tim Howard labelled jealous by fans after Pep Guardiola to USMNT take Donovan and Howard could rank as the two greatest players in the history of the USMNT, but the legends don’t think Pep would fit as the USA’s manager. Tim Howard: “He’s absolutely not the right manager for this team… Guardiola has only ever succeeded with tier-one players. People might get upset with this. We have probably tier-three players globally.” Landon Donovan: “Pep is a phenomenal manager, but this would not be right for the U.S. team. Would he be good for our 18-year-old players? I don’t know. We have good, elite players, but he’s been with the best.” Their take was ridiculed by fans of the USMNT, with many labelling them jealous, as a new era under Pep might lead to their nation-leading achievements in the sport to be forgotten. “The level of loserdom required to conclude that the winningest coach in the history of the sport wouldn’t be a “good fit” for your team is other-dimensional,” said one very angry fan . “I honestly believe these two dip—- want US soccer to continue to fail so they can continue to talk about their glory days…” said one fan calling out their potentially selfish reasons behind the take . “Best manager in the last 20 years? No, we don’t want him. Let’s bring in the Vancouver Whitecaps manager instead. What the —- are we talking about?” said another angry fan . “So the argument is let’s not hire the best manager in the world because we don’t know if he’s good at coaching bad players?” said one fan, lambasting their take with a laughing emoji . “They are so scared a USMNT might someday be better than they were; they actively are moving against the idea of hiring this generation’s best manager,” said another fan, implying they are jealous . Howard is the most capped goalkeeper in USMNT history, with the former Everton shot-stopper registering 42 clean sheets over 121 appearances. Howard holds the record for most saves in a World Cup game with 16 in 2014, one of the most iconic performances in USMNT history. Donovan is arguably the greatest player in USMNT history. His 157 appearances rank as the second-most, while his 57 goals are tied for the most, and his 58 assists stand alone as the most in USMNT history. Guardiola is the most-acco

item.title: Atlanta Dream star scores 22 points in her first game since losing WNBA finals
item.description: Photo by Kevin C. Cox/Getty Images Izzy Borlase is quickly proving why she’s one of the brightest young talents in basketball right now. At just 22 years old, Australian guard Izzy Borlase put together a really solid rookie WNBA season with the Atlanta Dream in 2026. Playing in all 44 regular-season games, she gave Atlanta a reliable spark off the bench, averaging 4.8 points, 1.5 rebounds, and an assist in 13 minutes a night. Once the playoffs hit, her role only grew. Across the seven-game WNBA Finals against the Golden State Valkyries, Borlase stepped up on the biggest stage, putting up 4.9 points and 2.3 rebounds a game, including a 12-point, five-rebound night in Game 3 and a huge second-half spark in Game 7. Izzy Borlase scores 22 points for Bendigo Spirit Izzy Borlase didn’t waste any time making her presence felt in her season debut for the Bendigo Spirit, helping lift the previously winless 0-5 squad to a massive 27-point over ladder-leading 5-1 Sydney. She set the tone right away, pouring in 13 points in the first half to send Bendigo into the main break up by 14. By the final buzzer, Borlase had filled up the stat sheet with 22 points, four rebounds, five assists, two steals, and a block. Before heading over to the WNBA, Borlase was already a star back home in the WNBL. She got her start with the Adelaide Lightning in 2022, quickly picking up Breakout Player and Sixth Woman of the Year honors, before joining Bendigo and taking home both the scoring title and league MVP in 2026. item.title: Cleveland Browns news: In search of an elusive victory
item.description: (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images Welcome to Week 10 of the NFL season. It feels like a long time since the Cleveland Browns last celebrated a win, but just three weeks ago, they opened their three-game road trip with a win over Tennessee. Since then, it was another disastrous afternoon in Pittsburgh against the Steelers, followed by last week’s overtime loss to the two-win New Orleans Saints. That is certainly no way to signal you are serious about staying in the playoff race in the AFC. Today brings a key turning point in the season for the Browns as they host the Houston Texans, who have won three of their last four games and enter today’s contest in second place in the AFC South. Two of those wins came against Tennessee and the Los Angeles Chargers, who enter the weekend with a combined record of 1-15. The other victory was a last-second one against Jacksonville, so it’s hard to gauge how good the Texans really are. The same can be said of the Browns, of course, as they have needed late-game comebacks in all five of their victories. This is a big game for both teams if they want to stay in playoff contention. And the Browns absolutely do not want to enter their bye week on a three-game losing streak. Keep it here at Dawgs By Nature throughout the day for all the pre-game, in-game, and post-game coverage as the Browns and Texans clash in downtown Cleveland. item.title: Phillies Send Johan Rojas Message Ahead Of PED Suspension Return
item.description: MIAMI, FLORIDA - SEPTEMBER 05: Johan Rojas #18 of the Philadelphia Phillies walks to the dugout during the third inning against the Miami Marlins at loanDepot park on September 05, 2024 in Miami, Florida. (Photo by Carmen Mandato/Getty Images) Getty Images The Philadelphia Phillies are once again evaluating avenues to improve their outfield production, after another disappointing season that saw one-year stopgap signing Adolis Garcia barely play. As president of baseball operations Dave Dombrowski returns to the drawing board to evaluate potential additions, he has provided an update on a once-promising franchise option who is nearing his last chance with the club. “We still like a lot of things about him,” Dombrowski said when asked about Phillies outfielder Johan Rojas, according to The Athletic’s Matt Gelb , “but he still needs to establish himself as a big-league player, especially from the offensive side.” FORBES | By Peter Chawaga Mets $22 Million Castoff Sends ‘Crazy’ Message After Surprise Trade Philadelphia Phillies Provide Johan Rojas Update After PED Suspension, Surgery Setback Rojas started in 189 games for the Phillies between 2023 and 2025, but struggled to become a consistent offensive producer even as he flashed elite defensive skills. Then Rojas’ 2026 campaign was effectively derailed before it had an opportunity to get underway when he received an 80-game suspension without pay after testing positive for a performance-enhancing substance. Then, while preparing to return from that suspension during this past season, Rojas hit a significant health setback and underwent season-ending surgery in June. “The procedure came a little more than a week after the club first announced that Rojas would require the surgery after feeling elbow discomfort while ramping up to return from his suspension,” MLB.com’s Paul Casella reported at the time . “The 25-year-old outfielder was serving an 80-game suspension without pay after testing positive for Boldenone, a performance-enhancing substance, in violation of the league’s Joint Drug Prevention and Treatment Program.” FORBES | By Peter Chawaga Cubs’ $68 Million Starter Castoff Jameson Taillon Makes Return Announcement Johan Rojas Faces Competition For Philadelphia Phillies Outfield Spot In 2027 Despite the difficult circumstances surrounding his latest season, Rojas will remain an option for the Phillies. “Johan Rojas, who was suspended for half of 2026 for using performance-enhancing drugs and then needed reconstructive surgery on his throwing elbow, is still in the organization,” Gelb confirmed. “He will play winter ball in the Dominican Republic, Dombrowski said. Rojas can be sent to the minors in 2027.” Barring another setback, Rojas will have an opportunity to demonstrate that he can contribute offensively while working his way back from surgery, but the Phillies are likely operating as if he’ll remain outside of the big league competition. item.title: “He Has No NFL Future”: Fans Refuse To Believe in Arch Manning After He Throws 3 INTs in Texas’ Win vs. LSU
item.description: Texas Longhorns quarterback Arch Manning - SEC Football Kickoff Media Day © IMAGN Texas Longhorns quarterback Arch Manning led a late touchdown drive to seal a 22-21 road win against the LSU Tigers on Saturday. Down by five with just two seconds remaining, Manning threw a four-yard game-winning touchdown pass to Raleek Brown. However, this did not mask his struggles. Manning completed 19 of 35 passes for 174 yards and one touchdown, but threw three interceptions. Fans expressed concern about Manning’s NFL future after his performance against LSU. “Late heroics or not, Arch Manning gonna get an NFL GM fired so fast,” one fan wrote. “Arch is starting to look like he doesn’t deserve to have the Manning name. Terrible performance,” one fan reacted. “Well, Arch is a bad QB that has no future in the NFL. If his last name wasn’t Manning, he be playing at Sam Houston St. instead of Texas,” one fan added. “Arch Manning is genuinely the worst quarterback of all time,” one fan said. Arch Manning Throws Three Picks Before Late Heroics in Texas’ Win Over LSU Arch Manning delivered a turnover-filled performance before coming up with the decisive play late in the game. The Longhorns quarterback’s turnover problems allowed LSU to take a 21-10 lead in the third quarter. However, Texas managed to turn things around. Manning started well with a 1-yard rushing score to cap the first offensive drive, giving Texas an early 7-0 lead. However, he was intercepted in the second quarter by LSU defensive back Ty Benefield, who returned it 33 yards and set up a scoring opportunity for the Tigers. Benefield picked off Manning again in the third quarter. LSU capitalized with a 44-yard touchdown run from Dilin Jones. Manning threw another interception with fewer than five minutes remaining as Texas tried to overcome LSU’s 21-16 lead in the fourth quarter. Manning launched a deep throw toward the end zone, but LSU cornerback DJ Pickett intercepted it. Manning redeemed himself by orchestrating a 12-play, 59-yard drive in the final minutes of the game. Starting from his own 42-yard line, Manning took the Longhorns down the field, capping it off with a four-yard touchdown pass to Raleek Brown. item.title: 'We've waited 73 years to be here' - Wales fans ecstatic after win over New Zealand
item.description: Saturday marked the first time Wales had beaten New Zealand in 73 years [Getty Images] Welsh rugby fans were "fizzing off their heads" on Saturday night after ending 73 years of hurt against New Zealand in an epic Nations Championship encounter. The match at the Principality Stadium ended 35-28 to the hosts as the All Blacks' run of 34 successive victories against Wales - dating back to 1953 - came to a juddering halt in Cardiff. Wales fans were left stunned by a result that came just a week on from having to grind out a win against Japan. Prince William, patron of the Welsh Rugby Union (WRU) also congratulated the team on the win, saying it was a "fantastic result". Three times Wales led by 14 points, and for the first time in history they scored five tries against New Zealand, but ultimately it was heroic defensive work that denied the visitors. All Blacks head coach Dave Rennie made eight changes from the side that swept past Scotland in their previous Nations Championship game. But the approach backfired spectacularly after a brilliant performance sparked astonishing scenes in Cardiff . A crowd of 55,152 could scarcely believe what had unfolded, and there were scenes of wild celebration with players in tears as Wales began taking in arguably the most famous win of their 145-year Test match history. Wales now holds The Raeburn Shield - a fan-created trophy that traces match-winners in men's rugby union back to the first international rugby union match in March 1871 [Getty Images] Prince William shared a post on Instagram saying it was a "fantastic result by the Wales rugby team". "My congratulations to the players, coaches and everyone who played a part - you have given fans across Wales a day they will never forget". Celebrities and politicians were also quick to pay tribute to the team for their heroics on the field. Speaking on 5Live Breakfast on Sunday morning , First Minister Rhun ap Iorwerth said: "Yesterday, meant a heck of a lot to us. "We are a pretty sporting mad nation. Rugby is very important to us as a nation. "The fixture against New Zealand is a particularly important fixture. We are a smallish country but in the rugby world, we are the biggest powers. He continued that "73 years we have failed to beat them, we have come close". "I have watched Wales come close some 20 years or so ago but sport is wonderful and awful at the same time. It became this psychological block. "Well, no more. That is it, we can go forward now with a new generation knowing that we can beat New Zealand." He said the crowd on Saturday "wasn't the biggest, but no doubt that changes". "I full expect the game next week to be a sell out." Gavin and Stacey star Jones shared her sheer delight in an Instagram video, with the actor looked visibly stunned following the incredible win over New Zealand. "This has been decades in the making. Huge congratulations to you all," he wrote on Facebook. "You should all be proud." Secretary of State for Wales Stephen Kinnock

item.title: 2027: Okpebholo’s 2.5m votes for Tinubu achievable says Afegbua
item.description: By Ozioruva Aliu BENIN CITY – THE Edo State Commissioner for Information and Strategy, Hon. Kassim Afegbua, on Sunday defended Governor Monday Okpebholo’s pledge to deliver 2.5 million votes for President Bola Tinubu in the 2027 presidential election, describing the figure as a target achievable through massive voter mobilisation and the state government’s development projects. Afegbua, who spoke on Arise Television’s Sunday morning programme, monitored in Benin City, said the target was based on the state’s growing voter population. He said that the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) had put Edo’s eligible voters at 2.865 million. The commissioner said the state government was determined to mobilise, sensitise and persuade voters to support Tinubu’s re-election, arguing that the administration’s infrastructure and social development projects had provided reasons for the people to endorse the President. He said, “The context at which we made that statement is the fact that we are setting a target for ourselves. After all, the new voters, as at last week when INEC released the figures, is 2.865 million people. What happens if we get 2.5 million? Is it a crime? “We are doing so much, we are working so much, we are building infrastructure, we are touching the social development aspect, we are building schools, health sectors, and all of that,” he said. Afegbua added that the government’s responsibility was to convince Edo voters to support Tinubu for another term, particularly because of the increased federal allocations to states. He said, “Our responsibility is to woo them, plead with them, appeal to them that they should allow the man who is providing the funding with respect to increase allocation to the state to continue so that they can see more development. “It is even dangerous for economic growth of any country for you to disrupt the flow or the process as it were now, when things are getting stabilised,” Afegbua said, adding that Edo was ready to deliver Tinubu in 2027. The commissioner disclosed that Okpebholo was expected to begin a tour of the state’s 192 polling wards to canvass support for the President, stressing that the government would work to ensure voters were mobilised and their votes counted. “Edo people are ready. We are going to deliver Edo State to President Tinubu, and we are very proud of it, and we are going to work assiduously,” he said. Afegbua also defended the Director-General of Tinubu’s Presidential Campaign Council, former Zamfara State Governor, Abdulaziz Yari, over his remark that Nigerians could still go to the market and find food to buy, urging a holistic interpretation of the statement. He said Yari’s position did not mean the country was without economic challenges, but that food remained available in Nigerian markets, unlike in some foreign countries experiencing grocery shortages. item.title: Tinubu’s economic reforms need continuity beyond 2027 – Jigawa Gov
item.description: By Muhammad Inuwa, Dutse ‎ ‎Jigawa State Governor, Malam Umar Namadi, has urged Nigerians to sustain President Bola Ahmed Tinubu’s administration beyond 2027, saying the ongoing economic reforms require continuity to deliver their intended benefits to citizens. ‎ ‎Namadi made the appeal on Saturday during the flag-off of the 2027 presidential, governorship and other elective positions campaign for the Jigawa North-West Senatorial District in Gumel. ‎ ‎The governor called on voters to support the All Progressives Congress (APC) candidates at all levels, from the presidency to the State House of Assembly, to ensure the continuation of policies and reforms introduced by the Tinubu administration. ‎ ‎He said the country needed to sustain the ongoing economic reforms so that their benefits could translate into improved livelihoods and greater economic opportunities for ordinary Nigerians. ‎ ‎Namadi particularly highlighted Tinubu’s agricultural reforms, saying the President was determined to make farming profitable again by ensuring that farmers earned meaningful income from their hard work. ‎ ‎”President Asiwaju Bola Ahmed Tinubu said farming must pay again. Not just hard work, but money in your pocket. That is the agricultural reform he is championing, and Jigawa will benefit from it,” he said. ‎ ‎He also urged residents of Jigawa North-West Senatorial District to give the APC another mandate in 2027, arguing that continuity would enable the party to consolidate its achievements and complete ongoing reforms. ‎ ‎Speaking on his administration’s performance, Namadi said his government had recorded significant achievements since assuming office in 2023. ‎ ‎Meanwhile, the APC Chairman in Jigawa State, Ahmad Garba, has declared that the party remains open to receiving members of opposition parties willing to defect ahead of the 2027 general elections. ‎ ‎Garba stated this while receiving 1,514 defectors from the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) during the zonal campaign rally in Gumel. ‎ ‎He said the party was ready to accommodate politicians and supporters from other political parties who identified with its leadership, programmes and political direction. ‎ ‎The APC chairman expressed confidence that the party’s achievements under Governor Namadi would continue to attract more supporters, urging members to remain united and intensify grassroots mobilisation ahead of the elections. ‎ ‎Speaking on behalf of the defectors, Malam Tijjani said the 1,514 members drawn from the 11 wards of Gumel Local Government Area joined the APC because of its people-oriented policies and programmes. ‎ ‎He assured the party leadership that the new members were prepared to work towards its victory in the 2027 general elections. ‎ The post Tinubu’s economic reforms need continuity beyond 2027 – Jigawa Gov appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Lamine Yamal set to wear number ten jersey for Spain in the absence of Barcelona star
item.description: Lamine Yamal set to wear number ten jersey for Spain in the absence of Barcelona star Lamine Yamal was a hot topic in Spain this week, after the forward missed out on the game against Czechia, leading many to criticise the national team for giving preferential treatment to the Barcelona forward. Luis de la Fuente, in the lead-up to the England game this evening, defended Yamal and stated no preferential treatment was given and that Yamal had picked up discomfort. De la Fuente further confirmed that Yamal will be available in action against England this evening. It promises to be a special evening for the Barcelona star as well, as he is set to don the number ten shirt. Yamal to wear the number ten jersey Yamal has been in electric form this season. (Photo by Alex Caparros/Getty Images) According to Diario SPORT , Yamal will carry the number 10 on his back as Spain take on England, with the opportunity seal top spot in their UEFA Nations League group, having all won all of their five games so far. It marks something of a change for Yamal, who has largely worn the number 19 shirt during his Spain career so far. Yamal won both the European Championship and the FIFA World Cup wearing the number 19 shirt for La Roja . This comes at a time when Yamal has become very synonymous with the number ten shirt at Barcelona, even dominating shirt sales and inspiring the newer generation, including the son of Declan Rice . However, with Dani Olmo, who wears the number ten shit for Spain, currently out injured, Yamal will be able to wear the number ten shirt for only the second time in his career. Not the first time for Yamal All eyes on Yamal ahead of Spain vs England. (Photo by Diego Souto/Getty Images) Tonight will not, in fact, be Yamal’s first outing in the Spain number 10. The forward previously wore it back on October 12, 2024, also in the Nations League group stage, during a narrow 1-0 victory over Denmark in Murcia. Dani Olmo was injured on the occasion as well. It will be interesting to see how Yamal performs in the number ten shirt for Spain, given that he had a relatively tough outing against Denmark in 2024.

item.title: ‘Finish This Guy’ – Asadula Imangazaliev Plans To Stop Aslamjon Ortikov In ONE World Title Rematch
item.description: Reigning ONE Flyweight Muay Thai World Champion Asadula “The Dagestan Ninja” Imangazaliev claimed the biggest victory of his career against Aslamjon “El Pantera” Ortikov . Now, the undefeated Russian wants to settle their rivalry in more emphatic fashion. The 23-year-old will defend his crown against the #1-ranked contender in the main event of The Inner Circle 39 on Friday, November 20, live in Asia primetime from Bangkok’s Lumpinee Stadium. The event will stream exclusively for members at live.onefc.com . View this post on Instagram Their first encounter at The Inner Circle 20 in June produced an unforgettable five-round war between two previously undefeated phenoms. Imangazaliev emerged victorious by split decision, becoming Russia’s first ONE Muay Thai World Champion while handing the Uzbek his first professional defeat. But the razor-close verdict left plenty of room for debate, with both fighters believing they had done enough to prevail. Now, with the ONE Flyweight Muay Thai World Title and a spot in the 2026-2027 ONE Flyweight Muay Thai World Grand Prix semifinals at stake, the divisional king is determined to demonstrate the difference between them. Imangazaliev told onefc.com: “I want to show how I can finish this guy, because it’s good that many people from Uzbekistan send messages supporting him. Of course, it’s no problem. “But I want to show my level. I’m on another level.” Photo Credit: ONE Championship Before facing Ortikov, “The Dagestan Ninja” had finished seven of his first eight ONE Championship opponents, establishing himself as one of the organization’s most feared knockout artists. Yet the Uzbek’s elusive movement and ability to survive dangerous exchanges presented a different kind of challenge. Having experienced that resistance firsthand, the champion wants his next performance to leave an unmistakable impression. He said: “I need to dominate. That’s why I accepted this rematch. It’s important for me to win, of course, and protect my belt, but I always go for the knockout.” View this post on Instagram The first meeting revealed just how evenly matched the two strikers could be. Ortikov constantly changed angles and found ways to disrupt his rival’s offense, while Imangazaliev pressed forward and answered with his unpredictable arsenal. The Dagestani has since worked with his team to refine his approach, believing that the lessons learned across their initial 15-minute battle could make all the difference in the sequel. Imangazaliev said: “We changed our game plan a little bit and changed our training a little bit. But he’s also good. He’s fast and a little bit hard to catch. But I think I have the key to this. “He’s also young. He has a little bit of the same style. He also moves so much, and he has good technique. That’s why it’s a hard fight. I need to relax a little bit more. I was too tight in the first fight. There are many small things that we need to fix for the second fight.” Photo Credit: ONE Championship Imanga

item.title: Rhode Island runners seize three New England crowns on historic day
item.description: It was a banner outing for the state at the 91st New England cross country championships , which were held Saturday, Nov. 14, in Maine. Bishop Hendricken's boys and Cumberland's girls brought home team titles, while Colby Flynn was the boys individual winner for the Hawks. Flynn crossed the line at Troy Howard Middle School in 15 minutes, 3.74 seconds, a few strides ahead of New Hampshire's Ben Groves and Connecticut's Tycen LaBelle. Bishop Hendricken teammate Shepherd Butler closed fourth, as the Hawks boasted five of the top 20 scorers who took the line in Belfast. Cecelia Ludwig was the top Rhode Island girl in the field, finishing in 12th place. The Clippers needed maximum effort from her and their other four scorers to edge New Hampshire's Exeter High by a single point. Anna Bianchi and Gabriella Stoothoff were both among the top 41 scorers, giving Cumberland depth their competition ultimately couldn't match. Bishop Hendricken totaled 53 points to outdistance New Hampshire's Coe-Brown Northwood (146), Vermont's Champlain Valley Union (181), New Hampshire's Hanover (189) and Connecticut's Xavier (195). It's the second straight regional crown for the Hawks, and it comes after comfortable victories at both the Class A meet and the state meet. Bishop Hendricken's win last weekend at Ponaganset Regional was good for its sixth consecutive Rhode Island crown. Watch RI high school games on the NFHS Network Flynn and Butler had plenty of support from their teammates, with six Hawks closing in the top 40 overall. Oliver Redmond (18th), Andrew Williams (28th) and Luke Tremble (33rd) completed the scoring while Jeremy Dru offered a bit of insurance. Bishop Hendricken will be primed for more competition to come in the coming weeks – Nike regional and national events are firmly on the program's radar. The Clippers totaled 128 points to close just one ahead of New Hampshire's Exeter, who compiled 129. La Salle finished third with 188 while New Hampshire's Hanover was fourth with 190 and Connecticut's Glastonbury rounded out the top five with 195. Ludwig was the state champion in 2025 and flashed some grit here while crossing the line in 17:57.28. Caylee Kurbec was 17th and Natalie Crawford was 40th before Bianchi and Stoothoof came home inside the top 70. Those two seniors added a first New England title for the school since 1977 to their four state crowns, and it was a first regional gold for Rhode Island since La Salle brought it home in 2015. Flynn, Butler, Redmond and Williams had more state company inside the top 28 on the boys side. Brooks Mello finished in 15th place for Barrington, and that comes after his Class B title and a top-7 performance last weekend. Will Souza came home in 19th place for La Salle and Leo Woodman crossed the line in 22nd place for Providence Country Day, adding a strong New England finish to his Class C crown. item.title: Pau Cubarsi names surprise Liverpool star as major inspiration alongside Barcelona legends Carles Puyol and Gerard Pique
item.description: FC Barcelona v Real Madrid - LaLiga EA Sports 2026/27 - Getty Images Sport Barcelona starlet Pau Cubarsi has named the three defenders who have shaped his meteoric rise to the top of world football. The teenage sensation, who recently tasted World Cup glory with Spain, revealed a surprising admiration for a Liverpool icon alongside two legendary figures from Camp Nou history. Cubarsi opens up on his inspirations after trophy-laden year Speaking in an interview with The Athletic , the young Spain international reflected on the figures who influenced his rapid ascent. The revelation follows an extraordinary year in which Cubarsi helped La Roja lift the 2026 World Cup while claiming the tournament's best young player prize. At club level, the teenager also recently secured the prestigious Golden Boy award , presented by Italian newspaper Tuttosport to world football's standout under-21 talent. Furthermore, he finished 12th in the Ballon d'Or standings as the highest-ranked centre-back and placed second in the Kopa Trophy behind Barcelona team-mate Lamine Yamal , who won the prize for a third consecutive year. Barcelona defender details admiration for Puyol, Pique, and Van Dijk When asked to identify his biggest role models, Cubarsi highlighted the contrasting strengths of two former Camp Nou stalwarts alongside his recent admiration for Liverpool's Dutch star, while explaining how he holds himself to high standards. “My role models are Puyol and Gerard Pique. I like both profiles: the gritty defender and the ball-playing one. Pique played more of a role in the build-up, but Puyol was key in terms of mentality and character," Cubarsi explained. “I have looked up a lot to (Liverpool’s) Virgil van Dijk in recent years. But I also tend to look at myself a lot and analyse my performances. “I am very self-critical when I make a mistake. During the game, you are aware of every action - whether you’ve been good or not. I am very self-demanding and beat myself up with stuff I can polish from my game, in a positive way. “Not that the next day I lose confidence - quite the opposite. I keep going with the same mindset and try to minimise mistakes.” Teenager calls for greater recognition for defenders Despite collecting major individual accolades, Cubarsi believes players in his position rarely receive the same appreciation as forwards. Celebrating his Golden Boy triumph, he admitted the honour validated his progress for both club and country. “When you’re young, awards like the Golden Boy or the Kopa trophy (the Ballon d’Or’s under-21 award) are dreams and I am so pleased to have won this one now,” he said. “It means our season with Barca and Spain was very good, but also that I am on the right track.” However, the youngster urged observers to value defensive contributions more highly across the sport. “Us defenders are not too eye-catching,” he said. “People prefer strikers or wingers, or anyone who scores and assists - and I get it. item.title: Giannis Antetokounmpo Makes Bold Statement on Heat’s Effort Following Blowout Win Over Pistons
item.description: ATLANTA, GEORGIA - OCTOBER 28: Giannis Antetokounmpo #7 of the Miami Heat looks on against the Atlanta Hawks during the first quarter at State Farm Arena on October 28, 2026 in Atlanta, Georgia. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and or using this photograph, User is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. (Photo by Kevin C. Cox/Getty Images) Getty Giannis Antetokounmpo’s first season with the Miami Heat has been played under a bright spotlight. It feels like every practice, every game, every press conference is being studied under a microscope. And following a rough 0-4 start to the season, many believed that newly finished ceiling was already ready to collapse. However, Antetokounmpo and his new teammates are showing the basketball world they’re going to be just fine. On Saturday night, Antetokounmpo and the Heat absolutely routed the Detroit Pistons, 137-117. After losing their first four games of the season, they have now won four straight games, the second-longest, current winning-streak in the Eastern Conference (Boston Celtics, 5). Giannis Highlights Great Team Effort Following Blowout Win And just as Antetokounmpo was required to answer questions last week on if he doubts his new team’s ability to win, now he’s able to answer questions on his team’s excellent effort. Antetokounmpo took this opportunity to make a bold statement, mixing in what appeared to be a veiled shot at the doubters from last week — who have since gone into hiding. “Just figuring out as a team, I think we just clicking better. We know each other’s spots better, and the most important thing out of all, we’re competing. Our effort is way better than the first four games,” Antetokounmpo said. The Heat now own a record of 7-6, and Antetokounmpo continues to be the superstar leader his squad needs. In the blowout victory over the Pistons on Saturday night, he dropped 34 points on 13-for-17 shooting from the floor. He added 14 rebounds, eight assists, three blocks, and one steal, playing one of his best games of the season. Saturday’s performance was his fifth game with at least 30 points and 10 rebounds. It was also his ninth double-double on the year. Most importantly, he’s remained healthy. Antetokounmpo has played in all 13 of the Heat’s games so far this season. This comes after he’d missed 61 total games over the past two seasons combined. Giannis Doubles Down on Heat Team-Effort As always, Antetokounmpo took the opportunity during his postgame press conference to highlight his teammates solid play as well. He mentioned everyone’s effort, and how they’ve done a great job improving after watching tape together as a team. He even points to Game No. 2 on the season, when the Heat lost to this same Pistons team 128-111. “We’re watching the clips before the game when we played them first, and we look like a whole different team. item.title: Wales suffer big Nations League blow in Norway as Erling Haaland extends record
item.description: Wales suffered a 3-1 defeat to Norway in Oslo to dent their hopes of staying in the top tier of the Nations League . Antonio Nusa and Andreas Schjelderup struck in the space of nine second-half minutes as Norway turned the screw. Substitute David Brooks halved the deficit 11 minutes from time as Wales finished strongly. Erling Haaland wrapped up Norway’s win from the penalty spot (Nick Potts/PA) However, Connor Roberts brought down Schjelderup and Erling Haaland converted from the penalty spot, extending his Nations League goals record to 23, as Norway avenged their October defeat in Cardiff. It means Wales will definitely finish bottom of Group A4, irrespective of Tuesday’s result at home to Portugal. Although they could finish on six points with Denmark and Norway, they have a worse head-to-head record against both nations – and could now face a play-off in March to avoid relegation to Group B. Both camps were aware of the extra incentive for victory as finishing third or higher in the group would guarantee top seeding in Euro 2028 qualifying, therefore avoiding the continent’s heavyweights. Wales made four changes from the side beaten by Denmark last month, with recalls for Karl Darlow, Joe Rodon, Liam Cullen and Harry Wilson. Rodon returned after playing just two minutes for Leeds since suffering a hamstring injury at the end of August. With the thermometer dipping below zero, Wales fashioned a real chance inside two minutes, but Wilson failed to properly connect with Brennan Johnson’s centre. Ben Davies cleared superbly with Haaland lurking at the far post, and Torbjorn Heggem volleyed over a presentable chance from the resulting corner. Antonio Nusa opened the scoring for the hosts (Nick Potts/PA) Ethan Ampadu was booked for tripping David Moller Wolfe, ruling the Leeds midfielder out of the Portugal game, but Wales were settling well. A lightning counter-attack saw Lewis Koumas and Wilson free Daniel James through the middle, but the winger opted for delicacy rather than power and the ball drifted wide. The stretching James was off target again as the visitors stifled Norway, despite the promptings of Arsenal midfielder Martin Odegaard who was operating in a quarter-back role. Haaland has been an isolated figure and Wales went close two minutes before half-time. David Brooks brought hope to Wales with his neat effort (Nick Potts/PA) Ampadu and Wilson were both involved as James fired low and hard to bring the first save of the contest from Egil Selvik. Visiting boss Craig Bellamy had warned of Norway’s set-piece threat and Nusa’s goal came from that source, although it was avoidable from the Dragons’ perspective. Rodon headed away Julian Ryerson’s 59th-minute corner as goalkeeper Darlow appeared ready to collect, and Nusa beat James on the edge of the area to find the bottom corner of the net with a fine strike. Wales suffered Group A4 disappointment in Oslo (Nick Potts/PA) Substitute Schjelderup doubled the lead from close range after bei

item.title: Texas A&M stock report, from Saturday's loss to Tennessee
item.description: Texas A&M suffered another disappointing SEC loss Saturday, falling 22-7 to No. 8 Tennessee at Kyle Field despite a defensive effort that kept the Aggies within striking distance for most of the afternoon. The Aggies (4-6, 1-6 SEC) entered halftime leading 7-6 after KJ Edwards broke free for a 25-yard touchdown run in the second quarter. However, Texas A&M failed to score again as Tennessee took control in the second half, scoring 16 unanswered points to secure the victory. Unlike last week's loss to South Carolina, when the Aggies moved the ball but couldn't finish drives, offensive production was a problem from start to finish. Texas A&M struggled to sustain possessions, leaving its defense on the field for extended stretches. The Volunteers managed just one touchdown, but five field goals were enough to overcome an Aggie offense that never found its rhythm. Several defensive performances and another strong running game offered some encouragement. However, the passing attack continued to struggle, and two late interceptions ended any chance of a comeback . With two games remaining, Texas A&M's hopes of reaching a bowl game are dwindling away, leaving head coach Mike Elko with difficult decisions about the direction of his offense. Here is whose stock rose and fell against Tennessee. Stock up: KJ Edwards Edwards provided the Aggies' biggest offensive highlight, breaking free for a 25-yard touchdown run that gave Texas A&M a 7-3 lead in the second quarter. The freshman showed his explosiveness when given an opportunity, but the Aggies couldn't consistently get him involved as the offense struggled to sustain drives. Stats: Seven carries, 44 rushing yards, one touchdown. Stock up: Tyler White White continued to be one of Texas A&M's most reliable contributors , helping the Aggies win the field-position battle at times despite their offensive struggles. His punting was particularly valuable in the first half, including a 62-yard kick that pinned Tennessee at its own 4-yard line. With the offense repeatedly going three-and-out, White was once again asked to do more than his share of the work. Stats: Highlighted by a 62-yard punt that pinned Tennessee inside its own 5-yard line. Stock up: Texas A&M defense The defense deserved a better outcome after holding one of the nation's top-ranked teams to a single touchdown. Tennessee repeatedly reached scoring position but struggled to finish drives, settling for five field goals. The Aggies also held the Volunteers to nine points through three quarters, giving the offense several opportunities to take control of the game. Stats: One touchdown allowed, five Tennessee field goals, nine points allowed through three quarters. Stock down: Marcel Reed Reed's struggles continued against Tennessee, as the sophomore quarterback failed to generate much through the air. The passing attack rarely threatened the Volunteers' defense, and Reed couldn't establish any consistency when Texas A&M needed to move the chains. Hi

item.title: College Football game between Louisville and UNC ends in heated on-field brawl
item.description: Louisville Cardinals ‘ 16-14 victory over North Carolina Tar Heels ended with a heated on-field brawl as players from both college football teams clashed after the final whistle on Saturday night. The incident happened in Chapel Hill after the Cardinals secured their fifth consecutive win. Players began exchanging words during Louisville’s victory formation before pushing escalated into several physical confrontations. The tension followed a crucial defensive play by Louisville. With 58 seconds remaining, defensive back Jabari Mack intercepted a fourth-down pass from North Carolina quarterback Travis Burgess. Mack returned the ball 32 yards before sliding to secure possession. Louisville then ran out the clock to claim the two-point victory. MORE: Landry Kiffin turns heads in stunning yellow minidress for final LSU home game However, the postgame celebration soon turned into chaos. North Carolina defensive tackle Xavier Lewis and Louisville offensive lineman Johnnie Brown III continued jostling after the final kneel-down. Other players soon joined the confrontation. Several pushed and grabbed opponents, while apparent punches were thrown during multiple skirmishes across the field. We got a brawl at the end of the Louisville vs UNC game pic.twitter.com/nIeyCwJuOc — gmannVOLS (@gmannVOLS) November 15, 2026 Louisville and UNC coaches react to the brawl Chapel Hill, North Carolina, USA; North Carolina Tar Heels quarterback Billy Edwards Jr. (9) looks to pass before the game at Kenan Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Bob Donnan-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters) North Carolina head coach Bill Belichick stepped onto the field to help separate players. One confrontation also spilled into the end zone, where another group became involved. Belichick addressed the incident after the game, making his position clear. “You play the game between the whistles, that’s not what we’re here for,” Belichick said. “We got out there and got everybody out as quickly as possible.” Louisville coach Jeff Brohm also expressed disappointment about the incident. “It’s obviously unfortunate,” Brohm said. “You try to get things broken up as fast as you can. It didn’t get broken up too fast, and you never want to see that happen. “I’d have to see what really started it. Hopefully we can correct that and not do that again.” MORE: When will college football AP Top 25 rankings release for Week 12? Poll delayed after FAA ground stop The Cardinals improved to 7-3 overall and 6-2 in the ACC. North Carolina dropped to 5-5 and remains one victory away from bowl eligibility. Louisville will host Pittsburgh next Saturday, while North Carolina travels to Virginia. Neither team nor the ACC has announced disciplinary action. — Enjoy free coverage of the top news & trending stories with The Big Lead Newsletter —

item.title: Ramla Ali Wins IBF and WBO Titles to Become Somalia’s First Boxing World Champion
item.description: Unified world champion Ramla Ali poses in the ring with her WBO and IBF super-bantamweight belts and her coaching team in Arlington, Texas. Photo Credit: Yahya Ali/Instagram British-Somali boxer and fashion model Ramla Ali is officially a unified world champion! On 8 November 2026 at the College Park Center in Arlington, Texas, the 37-year-old athlete captured the vacant IBF and WBO super-bantamweight world titles after securing a split-decision victory over American contender Mikiah Kreps . During the ten-round bout, Ali dropped Kreps with a sharp right hand in the third round—the sole knockdown of the night—before two judges scored the contest 97–92 and 96–93 in her favour, against one scorecard of 98–91 for Kreps. With this triumph, Ali became Somalia’s first-ever professional boxing world champion and a unified titleholder in one unforgettable night. Born in Mogadishu, Somalia, she fled the civil war as a child with her family and grew up in East London, initially taking up boxing in secret as a teenager before turning it into a life-changing calling. Ramla Ali makes her ring walk behind the Somali and British flags ahead of her super-bantamweight world title fight in Arlington, Texas. Photo Credit: Yahya Ali/Instagram Her remarkable journey from refugee to Olympic athlete and champion is also the subject of the biographical feature film In the Shadows. Directed by Anthony Wonke , the film premiered at the 70th BFI London Film Festival on 9 October 2026 before opening in UK and Irish cinemas on 30 October—just over a week before she lifted her world title belts in Texas. BAFTA-winning Top Boy actress Jasmine Jobson stars as Ali alongside Peaky Blinders actor Finn Cole as her husband and former coach, Richard Moore , with both Ali and Moore serving as executive producers on the project. This championship milestone builds on a string of barrier-breaking firsts across sports, cinema, and fashion. Long before her title win in Arlington, Ali made history as the first Muslim woman to win an English amateur boxing title, the first boxer to win an international gold medal while representing Somalia, and the first boxer to represent Somalia on the Olympic stage when she competed in the women’s featherweight division at the Tokyo 2020 Summer Olympics. Ramla Ali celebrates in the ring as the referee raises her hand following her split-decision victory over Mikiah Kreps on 8 November 2026. Photo Credit: Yahya Ali/Instagram Away from the ring, she has carved out an equally notable space in global luxury fashion. Ali has graced the covers of British Vogue, Elle UK, Harper’s Bazaar Arabia, and Grazia UK, served as a brand ambassador for Cartier and Dior, and made history as the first boxer to wear custom ring attire created by major fashion houses—including bespoke fight kits designed by Dior, Off-White, Versace, Alexander McQueen, and Burberry featuring the panther emblem from Somalia’s coat of arms. Now holding both the IBF and WBO super-bantamweight belt

item.title: UK tells Nigerian woman after 26 years to wait 20 more years for settlement
item.description: A 67-year-old blind Nigerian woman who has lived in the United Kingdom for 26 years has been told she may have to wait another 20 years before qualifying for permanent residency under proposed changes to the country’s immigration settlement rules. The woman, identified as Comfort, arrived in the UK in 2000 but lost her sight shortly afterwards after developing acute glaucoma. After spending 20 years in the country, she was granted permission to remain in 2022 under the long-residence immigration route. Under the arrangement, migrants are required to renew their visas every 30 months for 10 years before becoming eligible to apply for indefinite leave to remain, which allows them to live permanently in the UK. However, following new settlement rules announced by Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood, Comfort is likely to face an additional 20-year wait before qualifying for permanent residency, meaning she could be in her 80s by the time she becomes eligible. Concerned about her age and disability, lawyers at Refugee and Migrant Justice applied to the Home Office for her to be granted indefinite leave to remain immediately under provisions that allow exceptional cases to be fast-tracked. The application was rejected, with the Home Office initially telling her that she could return to Nigeria because services for blind people were available there. However, the refusal letter concluded: “Your circumstances are not so severe or lacking in potential treatment in India that it would warrant indefinite leave to remain in this case.” Comfort expressed disappointment over the decision, saying she had established her life in the UK and had no connection with India. “In 2022, I got my permission to stay here based on long residence in the UK,” she said. “I’m very disheartened that I may now need to wait nearly 20 years to get indefinite leave to remain. “I have been living in this country for 26 years. I have found my home here and settled well. I have my friends, my church and do voluntary work. I’m a good citizen, not a law-breaker and am begging the Home Office to have mercy on me and grant me indefinite leave to remain now, rather than making me wait 20 more years. “I don’t know why the Home Office said I could go back to India. It’s a country I have never visited and have no connection with.” Nick Beales, head of campaigning at Migrant and Refugee Justice, who is supporting Comfort, criticised the government’s handling of the case and the proposed changes to settlement rules. “This woman is blind, in her late 60s and has lived in the UK for a quarter of a century. She meets the rules to remain here and there is no public interest in making her continue to renew her visa. “Rather than viewing these vulnerable people as human beings, the government is fixated on appearing tough. item.title: What's next for SpaceX's Starship after epic Flight 15 chopsticks catch?
item.description: null Starship may have just made history, but it still has some work to do to get fully up and running. The megarocket launched on its 15th test flight on Friday (Nov. 13), aiming to pull off a dramatic and unprecedented twofer. SpaceX wanted to bring both Starship elements — its Super Heavy booster and Ship upper stage — back to the launch pad at its Starbase site in Texas to be caught by the tower's "chopstick" arms. It didn't happen with Super Heavy; the booster diverted to a Gulf of Mexico splashdown on Friday evening after experiencing a low-fuel alarm. But Ship came home successfully , nestling into the tower's arms in a soft and unprecedented embrace on Saturday afternoon (Nov. 14), 22.5 hours after lifting off. Long-distance view of Ship's historic landing on Nov. 14, 2026. (Image credit: SpaceX) SpaceX has caught Super Heavy on three test flights to date. But it had never caught a Ship before; indeed, it had never even tried before Saturday. It's tougher and riskier to catch Ship; the upper stage flies much higher and faster than Super Heavy, so its return trip is much more more involved. Saturday was therefore a very big day for the company. "That was the holy grail of spaceflight, plummeting through fire to be snatched out of the air by steel," SpaceX spokesperson Dan Huot said during the company's landing webcast on Saturday. "We caught a Starship, and now everything changes." The F light 15 mission plan gave us a sneak peek at the future: The double catch will be standard on operational Starship missions, as this recovery strategy will enable rapid inspection, refurbishment and reflight of the megarocket, according to SpaceX. And the company is indeed planning on rapid reflight. Elon Musk has said that SpaceX is targeting 10,000 Starship launches per year by 2030, which works out to more than one liftoff every hour on average. Why such a mind-boggling cadence? Because SpaceX plans to build megaconstellations far larger than anything circling Earth today. For example, it wants its next-gen Starlink V3 broadband network to consist of 100,000 satellites . And its planned Starmind AI data-center constellation will be 10 times bigger than that, featuring one million spacecraft , if all goes to plan. For perspective: SpaceX's current-gen Starlink network in low Earth orbit (LEO), by far the largest constellation ever assembled, is about 11,000 strong at the moment. A look at the 33 Raptor engines of Starship's Super Heavy booster during the vehicle's Flight 15 test launch on Nov. 14, 2026. (Image credit: Josh Dinner, Space.com/Future) Rocket recovery is only part of the reuse equation, of course; there's also refurbishment and reflight. And that gets us back to the "work left to do" discussion, for SpaceX has yet to demonstrate rapid reflight with either Super Heavy or Ship. item.title: NDLEA intercepts meth consignments from South Africa, hidden in cereals packs
item.description: **Arrest American Professional Basketball Player over Shipment of Loud. **Busts Gun Factory in Kaduna, Nabs Woman with 196 AK-47 Ammunition **Seizes Tons of Illicit Drugs After Raids in Lagos, Ondo, Delta, Edo, Osun. By: Kingsley Omonobi Fhe National Drug Law Enforcement Agency (NDLEA) said on Sunday that it’s operatives have intercepted 25.05 kilograms consignment of methamphetamine concealed in packs of assorted breakfast cereals imported from South Africa through the Murtala Muhammed International Airport (MMIA), Ikeja, Lagos, and arrested the 56-year-old trafficker who has lived in South Africa for over two decades under a stolen identity. In another interception at the same airport, an American professional basketball player was arrested over a 33.95kg shipment of Loud, a potent strain of cannabis, from Thailand, while a factory producing illegal firearms was busted in Kaduna while tons of assorted illicit substances were seized in raids across Lagos, Ondo, Delta, Edo and Osun states. Spokesman of the agency, Femi Babafemi said the meth suspect, Omokan Isaac Babatope, whose real name is Chinedu Onwude, was arrested on Wednesday 11th November 2026 at the arrival hall of Terminal II of the Lagos airport upon his return from South Africa. “A thorough search of his two travelling boxes led to the recovery of twenty-five parcels of a white crystalline substance, which tested positive for methamphetamine with a total weight of 25.05kg. “The parcels had been carefully concealed inside packs of assorted breakfast cereals and cereal-based food products in a bid to beat security screening. “The 56-year-old suspect holds both Nigerian and South African passports and has been resident in South Africa for over 24 years. “During preliminary interview, he confessed that he adopted the name Omokan Isaac Babatope after using forged documents to gain entry into South Africa and had continued to use that identity ever since. “He further stated that he was contracted by a South Africa-based man, Obiora Okoye, to deliver the illicit consignment in Nigeria for a fee of Twenty Thousand South African Rands (R20,000). Also, on Wednesday 11th November, acting on credible intelligence, NDLEA operatives at the MMIA intercepted a 28-year-old American citizen, Greene Da’monte Khiree, who arrived in Lagos aboard an Emirates Airline flight from Thailand via Dubai. The suspect, who was placed under discreet surveillance upon arrival, was observed abandoning his two checked-in bags before attempting to exit the airport with only his carry-on luggage. He was promptly apprehended at the airport car park. A search of the two abandoned bags, both bearing his name tag, revealed sixteen parcels of Loud in each, totalling thirty-two parcels with a combined weight of 33.95 kilograms. A tracking device was also recovered from the bags.
