item.title: Fela, Queen Latifah, Phil Collins Join Rock Hall Of Fame
item.description: Afrobeat pioneer Fela Kuti, rhapsodic hip-hop transformers Wu-Tang Clan and punk rocker Billy Idol were among the music luminaries inducted Saturday into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame at a star-studded concert gala. The versatile Phil Collins, post-punk and electronic dance music renegades Joy Division/New Order, and the velvet-voiced late Luther Vandross also joined the rock pantheon at the ceremony held in Los Angeles’s Peacock Theater. But several of the 2026 class of artists — Oasis, Sade and Iron Maiden — skipped the night celebrating their honor, one of the music industry’s most prestigious. But the show went on. Staten Island’s own Wu-Tang Clan — the ragtag group of New Yorkers who paired raw production with streetwise rhymes and martial arts influences — brought the ruckus, performing their own hits including “C.R.E.A.M” and “Wu‐Tang Clan Ain’t Nuthing ta F’ Wit.” “We went from being banned on the radio to the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame,” said member Method Man onstage to resounding cheers. To the haters, he said, “you can kiss my inducted ass.” It proved a banner night for women in hip-hop, with honorees including Queen Latifah as well as MC Lyte, who is widely recognized as the “First Lady of Hip Hop.” The storied performers tore up the stage with a medley of their hits, before Megan Thee Stallion and Remy Ma joined them to underscore the legacy of women in rap. Travis Barker, the drummer from Blink-182, inducted Collins, drawing tears from the British artist who attended the ceremony alongside his children, including Lily of “Emily in Paris” fame. US rapper/actress Queen Latifah attends the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame Induction Ceremony at the Peacock Theater in Los Angeles on November 14, 2026. (Photo by VALERIE MACON / AFP) Collins — whose entry into the hall is his second, the first was as part of the band Genesis — walked to the stage with two canes, taking the mic and saying, “I’m really not as bad as it looks.” “You haven’t heard the last of me, I can promise you that.” Cynthia Erivo belted out Collins’s smash “In The Air Tonight,” with Barker playing the instantly recognizable drum fill. “My life has just been one thing after the other, one dream after the other,” Collins said to journalists backstage. Oasis A ‘Dose Of Viagra For The Ego’ (L-R) Inductees Masta Killa, Method Man, RZA, U-God, Raekwon, Ghostface Killah of Wu-Tang Clan speak onstage during the 2026 Rock & Roll Hall of Fame Induction Ceremony at Peacock Theater on November 14, 2026 in Los Angeles, California (Photo by Theo Wargo / GETTY IMAGES NORTH AMERICA / Getty Images via AFP) Punk rocker Billy Idol performed on behalf of himself after an induction from Gwen Stefani, delivering an electrifying version of his hit “Rebel Yell.” Stefani later joined him onstage for a duet of “Eyes Without a Face.” Idol took to the podium with Steve Stevens, his longtime guitarist, who was also inducted. “Punk was and remains a tremendously positive thing. item.title: 2027: SERAP Gives INEC Seven Days To Prosecute Electoral Violence Suspects
item.description: The Socio-Economic Rights and Accountability Project (SERAP) has given the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) seven days to prosecute persons arrested over reported incidents of electoral and political violence ahead of the 2027 general elections or face legal action. SERAP made the demand in a letter dated November 14, 2026, and addressed to INEC Chairman, Professor Joash Amupitan, urging the commission to obtain relevant case files and investigation materials from the Nigeria Police Force and prosecute suspects where sufficient evidence exists. The organisation also asked INEC to direct its legal officers or appointed legal practitioners to review the files and promptly initiate prosecutions under the Electoral Act 2026. The demand follows several reported incidents of political violence across the country since campaigns for the 2027 elections began on 19 August, including the latest attack on members and supporters of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) during a town hall meeting in Oregun, Lagos, on 12 November. In the letter signed by its Deputy Director, Kolawole Oluwadare, SERAP urged Amupitan to press the police to conclude investigations into other reported attacks, arrest suspected perpetrators and their sponsors, and forward relevant evidence to INEC. It also called on the commission to exercise its powers under Section 83 of the Electoral Act 2026 to demand explanations from political parties suspected of involvement in or encouraging prohibited conduct and impose prescribed fines on those that fail to comply with lawful directives. SERAP expressed concern over reports of attacks on political convoys, party secretariats, rallies and meetings, as well as intimidation of candidates and supporters. Cited incidents included the reported obstruction of the convoy of NDC presidential candidate Peter Obi in Benue State on 8 September; attacks on political meetings in Enugu State on 12 September; and the attack on the convoy of ADC senatorial candidate Herberta Okonofua in Edo State on 6 October. Others included attacks on supporters of Accord governorship candidate Oriyomi Hamzat in Ibadan on 14 October, which reportedly resulted in one death, and the attack on the convoy of NDC candidate Rollins Offia-Nwali in Ebonyi State on 22 October, which allegedly left one person dead and three injured. The organisation also cited the reported attack on African Action Congress (AAC) presidential candidate Omoyele Sowore and his team in Ado-Ekiti on 30 October, the attack on Obi’s convoy in Calabar on 4 November, and an NDC procession in Asaba on 7 November, which reportedly left one person dead and five injured. It added that journalist Samuel Adebanjo was assaulted and his equipment seized while covering the November 12 incident in Lagos. item.title: Former APC spokesman warns of crisis if Tinubu is imposed in 2027
item.description: By Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA: Former Deputy National Publicity Secretary of the ruling All Progressives Congress APC, Timi Frank, has warned that any attempt to force President Bola Tinubu back into office in 2027 could plunge the country into crisis. Frank, who is the Ambassador to East Africa and the Middle East of the United Liberation Movement for West Papua (ULMWP), said Nigerians would not accept an outcome that contradicts their votes. “Nigerians will not accept a situation in which someone is declared the winner when the people know they did not vote for him. They should not push the country into a crisis by attempting to impose him on the people,” Frank warned. He urged the president to abandon his re-election ambition and guarantee a transparent electoral process. “Whoever wins should be allowed to emerge as the choice of the people,” he said. Frank also expressed concern over alleged attempts by some political actors to manipulate the electoral process. He described the public protest against Tinubu after prayers at the Shehu Shagari Mosque in Area 1, Garki, Abuja, last Friday as evidence of growing dissatisfaction with the administration. Tinubu reportedly faced boos from some Hausa protesters who chanted “Ba ma yi” (we don’t want you) after the prayers. In a viral video, some protesters were seen removing and destroying his campaign posters and billboards in parts of Area 1. Frank condemned the protesters for choosing a religious occasion to vent their displeasure and commended the President’s security detail for ensuring his safety and de-escalating the situation. He nevertheless urged the President to recognise the significance of the public reaction. “The rejection was total and unmistakable. No Nigerian president has been embarrassed like this publicly. The way Nigerians rejected him speaks volumes but should he decide to go ahead and he loses, he should be prepared to accept defeat just like former President Goodluck Jonathan did,” he said. The former APC spokesman said he was worried by what he called a growing gap between the assurances given to the President by political associates and the mood of the people. “I have seen the confidence with which some people are assuring President Tinubu that he will win the Federal Capital Territory FCT and that he is firmly in control. But the reported embarrassment he suffered during a prayer session in Abuja tells a different story. “What happened in the FCT last Friday showed that political assurances and promises are not necessarily a reflection of the reality on the ground. The public reaction reflects the anger and dissatisfaction of Nigerians, which those around the President may not be telling him about. “What happened in FCT and Jos after the APC rally has shown that people like the FCT minister, Nyesom Wike promising him 80 percent of votes in Abuja and the Governor of Edo State, Monday Okpebholo vowing to give him 2.5 million votes in Edo state, would disappoint him due to the reality

item.title: NGE demands release of detained investigative journalist, Ojukwu
item.description: The Nigerian Guild of Editors (NGE) has condemned the arrest, detention and prosecution of Daniel Ojukwu, an investigative journalist with the Foundation for Investigative Journalism (FIJ), demanding his immediate release on bail. The Guild also called for a review of the criminal charges against Ojukwu and FIJ founder, Fisayo Soyombo, warning that the prosecution could undermine press freedom and discourage investigative journalism in Nigeria. Ojukwu is currently being held at the Kuje Correctional Centre, Abuja, after being arraigned on a 12-count charge bordering on alleged cyberstalking and criminal defamation. In a statement dated November 15 and signed by its President, Eze Anaba, and General Secretary, Onuoha Ukeh, the NGE said it was alarmed that a journalist was facing criminal prosecution over reports raising questions about the expenditure of public funds by the Office of the Senior Special Assistant to the President on Sustainable Development Goals. The Guild said Ojukwu’s investigation reportedly exposed an alleged payment of more than ₦147 million, approximately $109,000, to an Abuja-based restaurant for the construction of classrooms and a skills acquisition centre at a primary school in Lagos. According to the NGE, the investigation raised questions about the existence of the projects, as well as the capacity and track record of the company involved in the contract. It described the issues raised by the investigation as legitimate matters of public accountability that deserved transparent answers rather than the prosecution of the journalist who brought them to public attention. The Guild expressed particular concern that Ojukwu had been remanded in prison despite pleading not guilty to the charges, while his bail application, initially scheduled for November 12, was adjourned until December 1. It said the resort to arrest, detention and criminal prosecution over journalistic work raised concerns about the commitment of authorities to press freedom, freedom of expression and Nigerians’ constitutional right to information. The NGE recalled its opposition to the alleged use of cybersecurity laws by the police and other security agencies to harass, intimidate and bully journalists. “Investigative journalism is not a crime. Asking questions about public expenditure is not cyberstalking. Demanding accountability from public officials is not defamation,” the Guild said. It maintained that public office holders must be open to scrutiny over their management of public resources, adding that journalists should not face threats of arrest, prosecution or imprisonment for reporting alleged irregularities. While acknowledging the right of individuals to seek legal redress over publications they consider injurious to their reputation, the Guild warned against using such rights to intimidate journalists or suppress legitimate investigations. item.title: AFCON 2027: 6 countries who need a win to keep qualification hopes alive
item.description: Six countries are facing an uphill battle to qualify for the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations (AFCON) after losing all three of their opening matches in the qualifying campaign. Lesotho, South Sudan, Somalia, Sierra Leone, Central African Republic and Liberia are yet to record a point after three rounds of matches, leaving them bottom of their respective groups . With three matchdays remaining, the six countries will need to turn their fortunes around quickly to stand a realistic chance of securing a place at the tournament. Lesotho occupy the bottom position in Group A after suffering three consecutive defeats. Their latest setback came against Gabon, who secured a 2-0 victory on Friday, November 13. The result left Lesotho without a point, while group leaders Morocco maintained their perfect record with a 5-1 victory over Niger to move to nine points. South Sudan are experiencing a similarly difficult campaign in Group B, having lost their third consecutive match following a 2-0 defeat to Angola on Saturday, November 14. The South Sudanese side are bottom of the group with zero points, eight behind joint leaders Egypt and Angola, who have both collected seven points. In Group C, Somalia are also struggling after losing 2-0 to Ghana on Thursday, November 12. The defeat marked their third straight loss, leaving them at the bottom without a point. Ivory Coast lead the group with nine points after beating Gambia 2-1, while Gambia remain second with six points. Sierra Leone are another country under pressure after losing all three of their opening fixtures in Group E. Their latest defeat came against DR Congo, who secured a 3-1 victory on Thursday, November 12, to maintain their position at the top of the group with nine points. Zimbabwe and Equatorial Guinea occupy second and third positions with four points each, while Sierra Leone remain bottom without a point. Central African Republic have also endured a disappointing start to their qualifying campaign in Group F. They suffered a heavy 4-1 defeat to Benin on Thursday, November 12, leaving them with three losses from three matches. Benin and Burkina Faso are joint leaders of the group with seven points each, while Mauritania occupy third position with three points. Liberia complete the list of six winless countries after losing 4-2 to Cape Verde on Friday, November 13. The defeat left Liberia bottom of Group K without a point, while Mali lead the group with nine points following their 3-2 victory over Rwanda. Rwanda are second with six points, while Cape Verde have three. Although the six countries have made difficult starts, none has been mathematically eliminated from the qualification race, with three rounds of matches still to be played. The fourth round of qualifiers begins on November 16, giving the struggling teams another opportunity to secure their first points and revive their campaigns. item.title: Iran attacks US military base in Bahrain
item.description: Explosions rocked Bahrain early Sunday as Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) said it had launched a drone attack on a United States military base in the Gulf nation. The attack came amid renewed hostilities in the Middle East, with Bahrain experiencing fresh Iranian strikes after a lull in attacks. Sirens sounded across the country, while authorities issued several emergency alerts on social media, urging residents to seek shelter. The warnings were the first since September. Bahrain, which hosts a major US naval base, has now been targeted twice in three days. The country’s military said it intercepted several Iranian attacks, preventing them from reaching their intended targets, while the Foreign Ministry confirmed that air defence systems had shot down Iranian drones. Explosions were heard around 4:00 a.m. (0100 GMT), according to an AFP journalist, while residents reported another series of blasts around 6:30 a.m. In a post on X, Bahrain’s Interior Ministry urged residents to remain calm, move to the nearest safe location and follow updates through official channels. Iran’s Revolutionary Guards said their Aerospace Force carried out the attack on a US radar system at a military installation in Bahrain. “The US air defence radar system at the Al-Riffa helicopter base in Bahrain was targeted by six drones belonging to the IRGC Aerospace Force,” the Guards said in a statement carried by Iranian state television and posted on Telegram. “The Strait of Hormuz is closed, and any aggression by the American enemy will be met with an even harsher and more forceful response,” the statement added. Iran has restricted shipping through the Strait of Hormuz, a major global oil transit route, during more than eight months of war, while targeting infrastructure including airports, seaports, energy facilities and US assets across the region. Bahrain condemns attacks Bahrain is among the Gulf countries that have faced thousands of Iranian drone and missile strikes since the conflict began on February 28. In a statement, the country’s Foreign Ministry rejected the use of its territory as a battleground in the conflict and held Iran responsible for the attacks and their consequences. Bahrain “rejects turning its territory into an arena for settling scores and holds Iran fully responsible for these attacks and their consequences,” the ministry said. On Friday, the Revolutionary Guards had announced that they targeted a US early-warning radar system in Bahrain, marking the first reported strike against a Gulf country since early September. The US military’s Central Command (CENTCOM), which oversees American military operations in the region, said it shot down two Iranian drones targeting the Gulf island, adding that the attack caused no casualties or damage. item.title: Ten years, thousands of staff and a billion dollars: the exclusive inside story of Grand Theft Auto VI
item.description: The latest instalment of the epic crime saga is finally here. We visit Rockstar Games for a hands-on encounter with the cultural event of the decade – and can confirm it more than lives up to the hype It still comes as a surprise for many to learn that Grand Theft Auto, the brazenly American crime series that has been one of the world’s most popular and most controversial video games for the past 20 years, is mainly made in Scotland. But if you grow up in Edinburgh, developer Rockstar North is part of the background mythology of the place. Plenty of people passed through this studio at some point or another in the 2000s, as game testers or employees. As a student in Edinburgh at that time, I would hear rumours of wild parties at the executives’ houses, as decadent as those in the game. At a bar or a birthday or a housewarming, you might meet a guy who claimed to have come up with one of the puerile puns that grace the in-game businesses (eg Nutsaki, a Japanese restaurant, or the fried-chicken chain Cluckin’ Bell). Grand Theft Auto is now made by a huge team of nearly 5,000 people around the world but its central nervous system is still in Holyrood, in the shadow of Arthur’s Seat. The setting of the latest Grand Theft Auto game really could not be further from the Scottish capital. Grand Theft Auto VI takes us to Vice City in the state of Leonida, a parody of Miami, Florida. It is a neon-soaked metropolis of sleaze and struggle, hard-partying excess juxtaposed with a barely concealed criminal underworld and unpredictable Florida madness. Continue reading...

item.title: Nigerian property owner in US named among worst landlords after building collapse kills eight
item.description: A Nigerian property owner, Olufemi Falade whose building collapsed onto an adjacent construction site in Brooklyn, New York, killing eight people, reportedly owes more than $450,000 in unpaid taxes, water bills and government fines. The property owner has also been listed six times on the New York City public advocate’s annual “Worst Landlords Watchlist” over allegations of poor property management. According to the New York Post, an examination of city records showed that Falade accumulated most of the outstanding debts through the three-storey building at 1321 Flatbush Avenue, which collapsed on Wednesday. The records indicated that he owes $170,000 in fines issued by the Department of Buildings in 2019 over improperly displayed signs, alongside $114,945 in unpaid water bills and $113,526 in property taxes dating back to 2021. Falade also reportedly owes the Internal Revenue Service $49,269 in unpaid personal federal income taxes, according to a 2010 lien, as well as another $4,316 in personal income taxes to New York State. The building, which had 98 outstanding violations with the city’s Department of Housing Preservation and Development before the collapse, reportedly had a history of maintenance and safety problems. The violations included a leaking roof, defective doors, bedbug infestations and exposed electrical wiring. Records showed that complaints over the leaking roof dated back to 1976, with further violations issued as recently as this year. Falade purchased the 96-year-old property in 1999 through an entity known as Femi Realty Corp. In November 2024, he transferred ownership to another company he controls, Isolag Realty Corp, signing the deed as both seller and buyer without any money changing hands. The report also revealed that Falade was sentenced to 12 days in jail in 2006 and fined $50,000 for civil contempt after failing to address more than 1,800 violations across 12 Brooklyn buildings he owned at the time. Meanwhile, questions have emerged over the approval of excavation plans at an adjacent construction site believed to have contributed to the collapse. The New York City Department of Buildings reportedly approved the excavation plans in March for a proposed three-storey, 25,000-square-foot mixed-use development at 2625 Bedford Avenue. However, the approved plans allegedly failed to provide adequate structural reinforcement alongside the building that subsequently collapsed. Real estate attorney Massimo D’Angelo, of Blank Rome, called for improved coordination between city agencies responsible for property safety and enforcement. item.title: Bishop Onah mourns four UNN students, commends Ortuanya’s leadership
item.description: By Alumona Ukwueze NSUKKA —The Catholic Bishop of Nsukka Diocese, Most Rev. Prof. Godfrey Igwebuike Onah, has joined the University of Nigeria, Nsukka (UNN), community in mourning the death of four students following a tragic incident at an off-campus house party. Bishop Onah, who paid a condolence visit to the Vice-Chancellor, Prof. Simon Ortuanya, on Friday, expressed sympathy and solidarity with the university community over the incident. He commended Ortuanya for his prompt response, particularly his efforts to establish the circumstances surrounding the deaths and his assurance that a thorough investigation would be conducted to determine the actual cause of the tragedy. The cleric expressed admiration for the Vice-Chancellor’s handling of the incident, noting that similar leadership qualities should be demonstrated at other levels of governance in the country. He also praised the Vice-Chancellor for identifying with the families of the deceased students and ensuring that the surviving students received necessary medical attention. While consoling the university community, Bishop Onah urged students to heed the Vice-Chancellor’s advice, abide by the institution’s rules and regulations and make judicious use of the opportunity to acquire university education. He further advised them to conduct themselves responsibly and remain focused on their academic pursuits, which he described as their primary reason for being in the institution. The Vice-Chancellor had on Thursday declared a three-day mourning period in honour of the deceased students. Ortuanya also visited the surviving students in various hospitals where they are receiving treatment, assuring them of the university management’s commitment to supporting their medical care and recovery. item.title: Insecurity: Forgive me for not visiting communities, Tinubu begs Plateau residents
item.description: President Bola Tinubu has appealed to residents of Plateau State to forgive him for not visiting communities affected by recurring attacks, particularly Angwan Rukuba in Jos North Local Government Area, following the March 29 killings. Tinubu made the appeal on Saturday during the All Progressives Congress (APC) presidential campaign rally in Jos, where he acknowledged the devastation caused by years of violence in the state. The president explained that his previous visit to Plateau was restricted to the airport, but insisted that he had seen the extent of the destruction and received reports on the situation from Governor Caleb Mutfwang. “When I last visited, the other time, I was limited to the airport; forgive me if you didn’t see me in the hinterland, but I saw the devastation,” Tinubu said. “I got the report from the governor; I saw the horror in the faces of our people. “At the end of the day, we are fighting together; it is now that we can rebuild, and I assure those displaced that we will rebuild your communities, and we will bring you back to your community.” Tinubu, who acknowledged that attacks in Plateau since 2001 had claimed lives, destroyed homes and displaced communities, assured affected residents that his administration would support efforts to rebuild their communities and facilitate the return of displaced persons. He also urged residents to embrace peaceful coexistence, saying differences in language and other identities should not divide them. “Living in different rooms and speaking different languages does not make us enemies of one another. We have to live together, we have to farm together, we have to build this Plateau and this country together,” he said. The president also expressed condolences to families who lost loved ones, survivors of the attacks and residents whose homes were destroyed or who remained unable to return to their communities. “To every bereaved family, every home destroyed, every survivor, and everyone unable to return home, I offer my heartfelt condolences for your loss,” he said. On March 29, several residents of Angwan Rukuba were killed when unidentified gunmen opened fire on people at a popular bar in the community. The attackers were suspected to be cultists. Following the incident, Tinubu, during a visit to Jos in April, ordered the deployment of 5,000 artificial intelligence-enabled surveillance cameras to strengthen security in Plateau State. During the visit, he sympathised with the victims’ families, saying no amount of compensation could make up for their losses. He also met with stakeholders and some victims at the Plateau airport. However, his failure to visit the affected communities during that trip attracted criticism from Nigerians, some of whom questioned his decision to restrict his visit to the airport. item.title: Police arrest suspected terrorism financiers, bandits’ motorcycle suppliers
item.description: By: Kingsley Omonobi The Police Force Intelligence Response Team (IRT) has arrested suspected terrorism financiers, alleged motorcycle suppliers to bandits, armed robbery suspects and suspected kidnappers in separate intelligence-led operations across Kaduna and Plateau states. The operations also led to the recovery of five firearms, comprising two pistols and three locally fabricated pistols, as well as a motorcycle and a stolen Toyota Corolla. The Force Intelligence Department disclosed this during a briefing on the operational achievements of the IRT in Abuja, saying the operations formed part of sustained efforts to dismantle criminal networks involved in kidnapping, banditry, armed robbery and terrorism-related activities. Speaking at the briefing, IRT Commander, Deputy Commissioner of Police Adamu Muazu, said two suspects, identified as Nura Umar, 20, from Kidandan, and Alhaji Rabiu Aliyu, 58, from Zaria, Kaduna State, were arrested over alleged involvement in kidnapping and banditry-related activities. According to him, the suspects were arrested on August 29, 2026, following intelligence linking them to the supply of motorcycles to bandits operating in Kaduna and Katsina states. The police said the suspects allegedly confessed to supplying several motorcycles to bandit groups in the two states. One Honda CV-125 motorcycle without a registration number was recovered during the operation. The police described the arrests as significant to efforts to dismantle the financial and logistical networks sustaining kidnapping and banditry, adding that investigations were ongoing to identify other accomplices and trace the financial channels supporting the alleged activities. In another operation, the IRT arrested three suspected members of a criminal gang allegedly involved in one-chance operations, car snatching and armed robbery in Kaduna and its environs. The suspects were identified as Abdullahi Abubakar, Yusuf Mohammed and Bala Ibrahim. Abubakar was arrested on October 12, 2026, at about 8:30pm, following intelligence linking him to a gang allegedly targeting residents, particularly commercial tricycle and motorcycle operators. The police alleged that members of the gang strangled their victims before dispossessing them of their valuables. According to the police, Abubakar, who had previously served a 13-year jail term for a similar offence, identified a suspected gang leader, Boniface, said to be currently in Kaduna Prison. The police alleged that Boniface directed Abubakar to a hideout where the gang’s operational firearms were kept. Following the execution of a reproduction warrant, operatives recovered two pistols from the location. Further investigations reportedly led to the arrest of Mohammed and Ibrahim, who were identified as alleged receivers of stolen vehicles, motorcycles and tricycles. item.title: Navy uncovers 56,800 litres of stolen crude in Rivers
item.description: By: Kingsley Omonobi The Nigerian Navy has deactivated two illegal refining sites and uncovered approximately 56,800 litres of suspected stolen crude oil in Ogbogolo community, Ahoada West Local Government Area of Rivers State. The operation, conducted on November 13, 2026, was carried out by personnel of Nigerian Navy Ship (NNS) Soroh, a unit under Operation Delta Sentinel, following credible intelligence on illegal refining activities in the Orashi Forest. Director of Information, Navy Captain Abiodun Folorunsho, disclosed this in a statement, saying the operation uncovered two illegal refining sites containing one refining oven, 22 dugout pits and four sacks of suspected stolen crude oil. According to him, the first site contained approximately 1,800 litres of crude oil, while the second held an estimated 55,000 litres. He said the recovered products and associated items were subsequently handled in accordance with established anti-crude oil theft procedures. Folorunsho said the operation underscored the Nigerian Navy’s commitment to dismantling illegal refining infrastructure and disrupting networks involved in crude oil theft. He added that the Navy would continue to deploy intelligence-driven operations to deny oil thieves access to the nation’s petroleum resources and protect critical oil and gas infrastructure. The Navy, he said, remained committed to sustaining operational pressure on crude oil thieves and illegal refiners in support of national crude oil production, economic security and the protection of Nigeria’s maritime interests. The post Navy uncovers 56,800 litres of stolen crude in Rivers appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: 2027: Umo Eno backs Wike’s Rainbow Coalition for Tinubu
item.description: Akwa Ibom State Governor, Umo Eno, has declared support for the Rainbow Coalition led by the Minister of the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), Nyesom Wike, to mobilise support for President Bola Tinubu’s re-election bid in 2027. Eno said he was willing to join any political coalition whose central objective was to secure Tinubu’s return to office in the 2027 presidential election. Speaking during a media chat on Saturday, the governor said he had thrown his weight behind the Rainbow Coalition, describing it as a platform for supporting the president. “That Rainbow Coalition is simply saying that we support President Tinubu as the president,” Eno said. He added: “If I will join and be a member of any coalition — whether it is Rainbow, call it any name. Any coalition that the central point is supporting the re-election of President Bola Ahmed Tinubu; I am for it.” The governor also said the relationship between the All Progressives Congress (APC) and the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) in Akwa Ibom State remained cordial, noting that both parties had reached an understanding on their political direction ahead of the 2027 elections. According to him, the arrangement involves supporting Tinubu, Senate President Godswill Akpabio and himself in the forthcoming elections. “I will work with all of them, and I think we are good on the ground in Akwa Ibom when it comes to the PDP-APC relationship,” he said. “We have agreed on the fact that we are supporting the president, we are supporting the Senate President, we are supporting the governor, and we have our clear understanding about those things.” BACK STORY The Rainbow Coalition, a cross-party political movement associated with Wike, has generated differing reactions within the APC, particularly over its implications for the party’s structures and candidates ahead of the 2027 general election. In September, APC leaders in the South-East backed the Progressive Governors’ Forum (PGF) in insisting that all party candidates should receive support in the 2027 elections. The leaders also rejected what they described as the “Rainbow (chameleon) Coalition”, warning that the party would resist any attempt to undermine its structures in the region. Their position followed the PGF’s declaration that it would not support any alliance or political arrangement capable of undermining Tinubu’s re-election bid or the electoral prospects of APC candidates. The governors were reportedly referring to the Rainbow Coalition, which Wike, a PDP member, has been promoting as a cross-party platform. In January, Wike said the coalition represented a departure from conventional party politics towards a collective political movement focused on advancing the interests of the state. Similarly, Imo State Governor, Hope Uzodimma, warned APC members in the state in October against working with political coalitions outside the party. item.title: 2027: ADC will defeat Tinubu in 13 Northern states – Amaechi
item.description: Rotimi Amaechi, the vice-presidential candidate of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), has expressed confidence that the party will defeat President Bola Tinubu in all 13 states of the North-East and North-West in the 2027 general election. Amaechi also predicted that the ADC would make significant inroads into the South-South and North-Central regions, specifically naming Niger, Kogi and Nasarawa states as territories the party expects to win. He spoke on Saturday at the ADC presidential campaign rally in Bauchi, where he warned that the party would not accept what he alleged was a repeat of the electoral events of the 2023 general election. “Because these people will do what they did in 2023. This time, we shall not agree. Do you understand? We will not do what?” he said. The former Minister of Transportation said the ADC had a stronger political presence across the North-East and North-West, which comprise 13 states. “We are the only party that comes with 13 states. The whole of North-East, the whole of North-West, that is 13, right? Let the president tell us how many states he comes with. He comes with only five in the South-West,” he said. Amaechi further predicted that the APC would lose another state in the South-West to the Allied Peoples Movement (APM). “That’s if he will. And the sixth state in the South-West will vote APM, whether he likes it or not,” he added. He said the ADC would challenge the APC in the South-South and North-Central, expressing confidence that the party would win Niger, Kogi and Nasarawa states. “We will fight with him in South-South. We will fight with him in North-Central. And be sure, be rest assured, Niger, Kogi, Nasarawa will be in ours easily,” he said. On the South-East, Amaechi dismissed the prospect of Tinubu making significant electoral gains in the region, insisting that the ADC would emerge victorious. “He will not go to South-East at all. Be rest assured, we will win. We will win. Things will get better,” he said. The post 2027: ADC will defeat Tinubu in 13 Northern states – Amaechi appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: US Thrash Haiti As Pochettino Prepares For Farewell
item.description: The United States thrashed Haiti 6-0 to surge towards the CONCACAF Nations League semi-finals on Saturday as Mauricio Pochettino’s penultimate game in charge ended in an emphatic victory. Goals from Christian Pulisic (2), Auston Trusty, Julian Hall, Weston McKennie and Folarin Balogun gave the US a commanding first-leg advantage to all but settle the outcome of the quarter-final before Tuesday’s second leg in Cincinnati. The build-up to Saturday’s fixture in Miami had been overshadowed by news of Pochettino’s departure as US coach after agreeing to take over Manchester United. But there was little sign that news of Pochettino’s exit had disturbed US preparations as they demolished World Cup qualifiers Haiti to deliver the biggest victory of the Argentine coach’s two-year reign. “Pochettino is an amazing manager, and he’s added a lot to us with the national team,” goalscorer Balogun said afterwards. “It’s always sad when you see a top coach leave, but it’s a part of the sport. “I think it was just important for us today to stick together and get the win — it just makes the send-off better,” Balogun added. Trusty gave the Americans the lead after just 10 minutes, confidently finishing from close range after Sebastian Berhalter’s free-kick from the right flank. Fans of Haiti cheer during the CONCACAF Nations League Quarterfinal match between Haiti and United States at Nu Stadium on November 14, 2026 in Miami, Florida. JC Ruiz/Getty Images/AFP (Photo by JC Ruiz / GETTY IMAGES NORTH AMERICA / Getty Images via AFP) That goal was all that separated the teams at half-time, but the floodgates opened after the break. Hall calmly tucked away Antonee Robinson’s low cross in the 52nd minute after a sweeping counter-attack to make it 2-0. Pulisic made it 3-0 from the penalty spot 10 minutes later after being brought down in the box by Haiti defender Carlens Arcus. The AC Milan forward then grabbed his second goal a minute later, rifling into the bottom corner from the edge of the area to make it 4-0. McKennie’s 68th-minute header put Pochettino’s side 5-0 up, and the US thought they had added a sixth soon afterwards when Balogun shrugged off Arcus to score from close range. Weston McKennie #8 of United States celebrates scoring his team’s fifth goal during the CONCACAF Nations League Quarterfinal match between Haiti and United States at Nu Stadium on November 14, 2026 in Miami.(Photo by JC Ruiz / GETTY IMAGES NORTH AMERICA / Getty Images via AFP) A VAR review, however, determined that Balogun had fouled Arcus in the build-up and the goal was chalked off. Balogun did not have long to wait, though, for his 13th international goal, latching on to a Malik Tillman through ball to score in the 82nd minute. AFP The post US Thrash Haiti As Pochettino Prepares For Farewell appeared first on Channels Television .

item.title: LEO gets a birthday bash, 75 years after clocking in
item.description: Business computing turns 75 this month, and Cambridge's Centre for Computing History is throwing a party for LEO, the machine that helped start it all. The LEO@75 event takes place on Saturday, November 28, from 10am to 5pm, with film screenings, historical displays, and hands-on activities for children. The Register has written about the Centre for Computing History a few times. It's an interactive computer museum just off Coldhams Lane in Cambridge, and back in 2018 it won National Lottery funding to help it "preserve, archive and digitise a range of LEO Computers artefacts, documents and personal memories." Admission supports the museum charity, with student and concession tickets at £10 and family tickets starting at £15. As well as stuff for the grown-ups, including a film screening, it will include events for smaller children (5-7) and a Python coding event for older (12-16) kids. Regular readers might recall our story about the Lyons Electronic Office back in 2021, celebrating its 70th anniversary. The Reg also published an obituary for Mary Coombs, the first female commercial programmer the following year. Coombs started programming LEO in 1952. Both stories offer more on the machine and the people behind it. LEO was an early computer, but from three-quarters of a century away, it's easy to miss just how early. Its design was based on Cambridge University's EDSAC, developed by a team led by the late, great Sir Maurice Wilkes. The Reg mentioned EDSAC in our obituary for Wilkes, and went into more detail for his centenary in 2013 . It also crops up in our Geek's Guide to Cambridge . The design of EDSAC was directly inspired by John von Neumann's famous, and incomplete, "First Draft of a Report on the EDVAC" – which The Reg talked about in 2011 . The draft report was circulated in 1945, based on the proposal for EDVAC, four years before the hardware was delivered. That was also the year John Mauchly and J. Presper Eckert completed its predecessor, ENIAC. In its original form, ENIAC was programmed by setting switches and reconnecting cables; EDVAC, by contrast, was designed to store its instructions in memory. The report set out what's now called the "von Neumann architecture." Wilkes and Douglas Hartree drew on those ideas in developing EDSAC, LEO's immediate forerunner and one of the world's earliest practical stored-program computers. The first working electronic stored-program machine was the Manchester "Baby," the Small-Scale Experimental Machine, which ran its first program in 1948 . EDSAC ran its first program in May 1949 – a few months before the delivery of BINAC, Eckert and Mauchly's first stored-program machine. LEO ran its first commercial application in 1951. That was also the year the US Census Bureau took delivery of Eckert and Mauchly's UNIVAC I . ®

item.title: CHINA DIARIES: The Future of farming
item.description: When we talk about China’s development, the images that often come to mind are high-speed trains, towering skyscrapers, electric vehicles and impressive infrastructure. But there is another quiet revolution taking place, one that is just as important to China’s future: agriculture. I had an opportunity to explore this during a visit to Yangling, in Shaanxi Province, a place that has become an important centre for agricultural science, research, innovation and technology. Our visit took us to three facilities: the SCO Demonstration Base for Agricultural Technology Exchange and Training, the Yangling Smart Agriculture Demonstration Park, and Yangling Liangke Agricultural Science and Technology Co. Ltd. What I saw offered an interesting glimpse into how China is using science and technology to rethink farming, improve productivity and strengthen food security. China Diaries: An Emperor, 8,000 Soldiers and a Lesson for Nigeria! 2027: We’ll fight Tinubu in South, North-Central, sweep North-West, North-East – Amaechi And, naturally, it got me thinking about Nigeria. Where farming meets the digital age One of the most interesting parts of the visit was seeing how technology is being integrated into everyday agricultural activities. At the smart agriculture demonstration facility, I saw a control station where plants are monitored through screens. Rather than relying entirely on physical observation, information about growing conditions can be monitored centrally, allowing operators to keep track of what is happening inside the growing facilities. It was a reminder that modern farming is increasingly becoming a data-driven activity. The farmer of the future may still walk through the farm, inspect the crops and get his hands dirty, but technology is giving him additional tools to make better decisions. I also saw vegetables being cultivated indoors in a controlled environment. It was fascinating to see food production taking place in a setting that looked quite different from the conventional farms we are familiar with in Nigeria. The idea is to manage growing conditions and create a more controlled environment for production. Such systems can help reduce dependence on some external weather conditions and make production more predictable, although their commercial viability depends on energy, infrastructure and operating costs. Another interesting sight was the display of grains and seedlings. These may look ordinary at first glance, but they represent an important part of the agricultural value chain: research, seed development and the effort to improve the quality and productivity of crops before they even get to the farm. Then came the agricultural drones. I photographed drones designed to spray farmland. Their use illustrates how technology can help farmers cover large areas more efficiently and apply agricultural treatments with greater precision. Of course, drones require trained operators, maintenance and appropriate regulation, but th

item.title: SpaceX returned its Starship rocket on Saturday—but there's a catch
item.description: STARBASE, Texas —The black and silver ship fell out of the sky, emerging from the cloud deck near the very end of its flight. Incongruously, the rocket flew horizontal until the last moment when three Raptor rocket engines ignited and it swooped into a vertical position. Slowly, gently, haltingly, the Starship upper stage eased its way toward the waiting tower where two arms extended outward, awaiting expectantly. The margins are so incredibly narrow. Two nubs on either side of the rocket, each protruding only about one foot, were the only purchase the rocket would have on the arms. Then, less than a minute after it came into view, the Starship upper stage was snagged by the launch tower, as snug as you like. And so it was all over. SpaceX, nearly a quarter of a century after its founding, had just taken a hugely significant step toward developing and optimizing a massive, rapidly reusable rocket. Read full article Comments

item.title: Magic: The Gathering is getting a Netflix animated series. For real this time.
item.description: "It's really happening. I promise. For real." Those are the first words from Roy Graham, Head of Story at Magic: The Gathering , in a video posted yesterday announcing Planeswalker , the animated series heading to Netflix in 2027. item.title: This Week In Space podcast: Episode 236 — Alienspotting
item.description: null On Episode 236 of This Week In Space , Tariq Malik and Rod Pyle are joined by Mikhail Tikhonov to talk about how life can take more unusual forms, ones we might not even recognize. When we think of extraterrestrials, our minds generally go from the latex-suited bipedal aliens seen in Star Trek and Star Wars to more exotic critters in sci-fi movies. Scientists think in terms of carbon-based microbial life and other lower life forms. But some researchers, such as Tikhonov from Washington University, suggest that life can take more unusual forms, ones we might not even recognize. He further suggests a new definition of life: something that takes in and transforms energy and replicates. His ideas radically expand our notions of alien life and how it might be recognized. item.title: Bitcoin Price Falls 14% in a Week to $65,000 as Weekend Selling Breaks Friday’s Low
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine Bitcoin Price Falls 14% in a Week to $65,000 as Weekend Selling Breaks Friday’s Low Bitcoin price crashed about 14% over the past week and was trading near $65,200 on Saturday morning after sliding to about $65,000, according to Bitcoin Magazine Pro data. The move broke below Friday’s low of about $67,555 and marked the weakest level since mid-August, as weekend trading extended a selloff that has followed a stronger dollar and a fully priced December Federal Reserve rate hike. A week ago, on Nov. 7, bitcoin was trading near $75,750. The decline steepened after Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang resigned on Thursday, a shake-up that caused AI stocks to sell off which could potentially be responsible for sending bitcoin below $72,000. It slipped toward $71,000 by Thursday evening, then crashed to about $67,555 around midnight Eastern on Friday, its lowest level since August, before recovering toward $69,800 in the morning. A brief pop above $70,000 after the producer-price report faded, and the bitcoin price spent Friday afternoon pinned below $70,000, near $68,900. Selling resumed Friday evening and carried into the mid-$66,000s. Bitcoin briefly steadied overnight near $67,000, then sold off again after 8 a.m. ET Saturday, reaching that $65,500 low in the 10 a.m. hour and taking out Friday’s trough. A stronger dollar and higher yields still weigh on the bitcoin price The Labor Department said Friday that the Producer Price Index for final demand rose 0.3% in October, short of the 0.4% increase economists had expected. On an unadjusted basis, the index was up 6.5% from a year earlier, the largest 12-month rise since November 2022. The slightly cooler monthly figure lifted bitcoin above $70,000 for only minutes. Bond traders were unconvinced. The 10-year Treasury yield climbed as high as 5.17% on Friday, a four-week high, and closed at 5.15%. The U.S. dollar index held at a 19-month high, its strongest level since April 2025. Boston Fed President Susan Collins said Friday that “soon, some additional tightening of Fed monetary policy may be appropriate,” and San Francisco Fed President Mary Daly said policymakers will, “in all likelihood, raise interest rates.” Higher rates raise the cost of holding an asset that pays no interest, and a stronger dollar has weighed on the bitcoin price for much of November. Traders fully priced a quarter-point hike at the Fed’s Dec. 8-9 meeting, CME FedWatch data show. Chip stocks offered no cushion. The iShares Semiconductor ETF fell more than 3% on Friday, and Advanced Micro Devices dropped more than 8%. The Nasdaq 100 closed down 1.22%. U.S. stock and bond markets are closed Saturday, but those levels still frame the weekend session. Nvidia is due to report third-quarter results on Tuesday under interim CEO Colette Kress, the first earnings release since Huang stepped down. ETF outflows continue as mining difficulty drops Demand from spot bitcoin ETFs has not filled the gap. BlackRock’s iShares B

item.title: The OpenAI board member who fired Sam Altman says we still can’t trust AI CEOs
item.description: Today, I’m talking with Helen Toner, the executive director of the Center for Security and Emerging Technology at Georgetown University. This episode is part two of our series on AI in real life. Helen is a well-known figure in the AI safety and policy community, though she is perhaps best known for having served on the board of OpenAI, when she was one of four board members who voted to fire Sam Altman . That incident, now sometimes referred to as “the blip,” ended with Sam coming back as CEO, Helen resigning, and a new board of directors. OpenAI has since restructured entirely . But it’s worth remembering what Helen and the board were supposed to do: OpenAI’s nonprofit board existed specifically to make sure the company didn’t betray its mission to build safe AI by prioritizing profit and growth over safety. When the board actually tried to pull the lever, that accountability mechanism broke, and here we are. Verge subscribers, don’t forget you get exclusive access to ad-free Decoder wherever you get your podcasts. Head here . Not a subscriber? You can sign up here . Now, the question of AI safety is everywhere . This summer, AI models from OpenAI and Anthropic broke out of their testing environments and hacked real companies. The CEOs of these frontier labs have since called for a slowdown and asked Washington for help, but the White House’s answer was a voluntary accord — one that relies in part on the kind of board accountability that failed at OpenAI. Anthropic is also about to go public, which will put a whole new set of market pressures on OpenAI’s biggest competitor. Helen has seen up close what happens when safety commitments run headlong into commercial incentives. And as she put it to me, if our hopes for the future depend on any one person being trustworthy, we’re in big trouble. So we talked about what we might do instead: what the labs are actually trying to build, whether AI alignment is a problem that can be solved, and what a smarter approach to AI regulation might look like. That includes how to think about China, which is the issue that looms large in every policy conversation about AI right now — especially now after the Jensen Huang affair . Just for clarity, Helen and I talked before Nvidia opened its investigation and Jensen ultimately resigned, so you won’t hear us talk about that directly. Before we get going, do me a favor and subscribe to Decoder on YouTube , where we put out new episodes every Monday and Thursday. Okay: Helen Toner, the executive director of CSET, on the future of AI safety. Here we go. This interview has been lightly edited for length and clarity. Helen Toner, you’re the executive director for the Center for Security and Emerging Technology at Georgetown University. Welcome to Decoder . Thanks so much. Great to be here. I have wanted to talk to you for 10 million years. I am so excited you’re here. You’ve been involved in a lot of AI safety and ethics ideas for a long time. You were obviously on the

item.title: 'Alien: Fireteam Elite 2' is a good old-fashioned bug hunt, ironically plagued by bugs
item.description: The first Aliens: Fireteam Elite was among my favorite Alien video games , and there were a lot of reasons to be excited for a sequel. At Summer Game Fest 2026 , we learned of many smart changes and improvements to the formula, and I was eager to go bug-hunting again. A new campaign, fully reworked classes, and four-player co-op. What could go wrong? Months later, Aliens: Fireteam Elite 2's debut has been difficult, mostly due to glaring tech issues. Despite this, it's still a welcome jolt of action for a franchise that's been focusing on making the Xenomorphs scary again in recent years. Alien: Romulus (2024) and Alien: Earth (2025) have reestablished the acid-blooded Xenomorphs as bona fide horror icons, while games like Aliens: Dark Descent bet on tense real-time tactics and squad management; Rogue Incursion spooked VR and non-VR players alike; and we even have Isolation 2 's pure survival horror to look forward to. Rough edges aside, Aliens: Fireteam Elite 2 is a necessary return to mindless shooting and treating the Xenos as a relentless horde, dropping the stalking and slasher-inspired murders in favor of sci-fi shootouts and macho one-liners. It's far from a novel idea — even the original game is only five years old — but a classic for a reason. Another glorious day in the Corps (Image credit: Daybreak Game Company) Believe it or not, another colony has fallen prey to the Xenomorphs in Fireteam Elite 2. The familiar setup takes a new team of Colonial Marines to a mining facility on LV-558, where contact has been lost with the first wave of Marines that went in to deal with the threat. This isn't first contact; the Marines are more than used to bug hunts by now, which means there's less exposition to cut through before getting to the Xeno-blasting chaos. The writing certainly won't stun the Academy (and there's definitely too much of it in between missions), but the agility here is appreciated. We've fought these aliens many, many times before. Fireteam Elite 2 is smart enough to sidestep fake tension and just hit the ground running. (Image credit: Daybreak Game Company) All the design changes and upgrades reinforce the intent to make the ultimate Aliens action game. Classes have more defined roles and access to better, more destructive sci-fi weapons, and the upgrade to four-player fireteams is welcome when aliens and hostile synths won't stop pouring in. Tired of replaying campaign missions on higher difficulties and with modifiers? Prepare for the worst in this shooter's version of the classic horde mode. At its best, Aliens: Fireteam Elite 2 understands why James Cameron's masterpiece still holds up. During the biggest Xenomorph onslaughts — when the bullets are flying and acid is spraying — the game's shortcomings and jankier elements fade away. Game over, man (Image credit: Daybreak Game Company) There are still some scares hiding in here, though, ready to make complacent players jump out of their seats. Special Xenomorphs

item.description:
Tariq is the Editor-in-Chief of Space.com based out of our New York City office and joined the team in 2001, first as an intern and staff writer, and later as an editor. He covers human spaceflight, exploration and space science, as well as skywatching and entertainment. He became Space.com's Managing Editor in 2009 and Editor-in-Chief in 2019. In October 2022, Tariq received the Harry Kolcum Award for excellence in space reporting from the National Space Club Florida Committee. In June 2025, the National Space Society awarded him the Space Pioneer Award for Excellence in Mass Media at the International Space Development Conference in Orlando, Florida.

Hailing from Stockton, California (where he attended the same high school as NASA astronaut Jose Hernandez), Tariq studied print journalism and astronomy at the University of Southern California in Los Angeles, earning a bachelor's degree in journalism in 1999 along with a minor in astronomy. He then served as a staff reporter for The Los Angeles Times covering education and city beats in La Habra and Fullerton in Orange County for the Our Times sections.

In 2000, Tariq became the city reporter for the Huntington Beach Independent, a weekly publication of the Los Angeles Times, covering local politics and events, crime, business and environmental issues. He left the Los Angeles Times in 2001 to study science journalism at New York University, where he earned a master's degree in 2002 from NYU's Science and Environmental Reporting Program (now the Science, Health and Environmental Reporting Program) under the direction of space reporter William Burrows.

Tariq first joined Space.com as an intern in September 2001 while also serving as a research assistant for nutrition writer Gary Taubes and writing freelance projects, where his work appeared in The Scientist and Laboratory Equipment Magazine. He became a full-time reporter covering spaceflight in 2004, with this first launch being NASA's STS-114 Return to Flight mission in July 2005.

Tariq is also an Eagle Scout (yes, he has the Space Exploration merit badge) and went to Space Camp four times as a kid and a fifth time as an adult. When not writing about space, you can find Tariq watching the latest Star Trek TV series, sci-fi movies and reading about hippos, his favorite animal. You can find Tariq at Space.com and as the co-host to the This Week In Space podcast with space historian Rod Pyle on the TWiT network. To see his latest project, you can follow Tariq on Twitter @tariqjmalik.

item.title: On this day in space! Nov. 14, 1969: NASA's Apollo 12 astronauts launch to the moon on a 'pinpoint landing' lunar mission
item.description: null On Nov. 14, 1969, the Apollo 12 mission launched to the moon. This was the second moon landing of the Apollo program. The two astronauts on board were Pete Conrad , commander, and Alan Bean , the lunar module pilot. Astronaut Richard Gordon , the command module pilot, stayed in the command module and orbited the moon while his crewmates went to the surface. The astronauts made a pinpoint landing in a lunar mare called the Ocean of Storms. The previous moon mission, Apollo 11 , drifted far from the planned landing zone. But Apollo 12 landed close to a scientific target. That target was a robotic lander called Surveyor 3 . Scientists wanted to look at Surveyor 3 to see how well the spacecraft lasted on the moon since it landed there more than two years earlier. The Apollo 12 moonwalkers also performed a lot of moon science. The astronauts picked up 75 pounds of moon rocks. Most of the rocks were basalts that formed from molten lava. These basalts showed the Apollo 12 landing site is more than 3 billion years old. The Apollo 12 astronauts on NASA's second crewed moon landing mission. They are (left to right) are Charles Conrad Jr., Richard F. Gordon Jr., and Alan L. Bean. (Image credit: NASA) Why it mattered Apollo 12 proved that the Apollo 11 moon landing was not just a one-off stunt while setting the stage for even more ambitious missions. To truly explore the moon and advance our understanding of how our solar system formed, the follow-on Apollo flights needed to be able to land where the geologists had identified as areas of interest. Apollo 12, with its touchdown in proximity to the Surveyor probe, proved this was possible. The Apollo 12 astronauts visited NASA's Surveyor 3 lander and took samples of it back to Earth. (Image credit: NASA) The launch of Apollo 12 also underscored the importance of having a well-prepared Mission Control team, an asset that would be critical to outcome of the next mission, Apollo 13. The ability to recover from a complete electrical short out with the simple call of a through of a switch "SCE to AUX" proved that knowing every detail about how the spacecraft worked was key to a successful program. Want more space history? Check out our full On This Day In Space Story archive and watch our On This Day In Space videos on YouTube .

item.title: Mark Your Calendars! Lagos International Theatre Festival Returns to MUSON Centre This November
item.description: The Lagos International Theatre Festival ( LITF ) returns for its 2026 edition on November 14–15 at the MUSON Centre, Lagos, bringing together an exciting programme of theatre from Nigeria and around the world. The festival, which attracts more than 25,000 attendees across its programme days, has become one of the most anticipated events on Lagos’s cultural calendar. This year’s festival is themed “The Masks We Wear”, anchored by the statement “The Stage Is Everywhere.” The theme explores the different roles and identities people assume in everyday life, while inviting audiences to consider how theatre extends beyond the traditional stage. LITF 2026 brings an international dimension to Lagos, featuring artists and productions from Kenya, Canada and Brazil alongside a diverse Nigerian programme. An international highlight is LeRa Entertainments’ Under The Mango Tree from Canada, produced by Lennette Randall , with productions from Norway, Kenya and Brazil adding further cultural and theatrical perspectives. The Nigerian programme features productions from Lagos, Abuja, Enugu and Abeokuta, including Monkey Laundry , directed by Olarotimi Fakunle ; tHERapy , directed by Tosin Adeyemi ; What You Have Become , directed by Lanre Adediwura; and Behind Closed Doors , directed by Bolanle Austen-Peters. The festival will also spotlight emerging theatre makers through productions from Atlantic Hall, Evergreen College and Children’s International School, alongside professional and independent productions. The festival experience begins ahead of the main weekend with a series of events across Lagos. On November 9, Theatre Meets Food, hosted by Hilda Baci, will bring together artists, partners, cultural leaders and members of Lagos’s creative community for an evening of food, theatre and conversation. This will be followed by Embassy Nights on November 10 and 11, celebrating international cultural exchange among diplomatic representatives, artists and creative industry leaders. The programme culminates in an Opening Night Gala on November 13, ahead of the main festival weekend at MUSON Centre on November 14 and 15. LITF 2026 is supported by the Lagos State Government, LekOil, Pillar Oil, Afrexim and Amstel , alongside its growing network of international and cultural partners. Founder of LITF, Bolanle Austen-Peters , said: “The Masks We Wear is a theme that speaks to all of us. We all play different roles in our lives, and theatre allows us to examine those roles, question them, and perhaps see ourselves differently. This year, we are also reminding audiences that theatre is not confined to a theatre building. The stage is everywhere.” Festival Director, Vanessa Jev , said the diversity of voices at this year’s festival was particularly exciting, with Nigerian artists joining performers from Kenya, Canada and Brazil to create opportunities for audiences to experience different cultures and perspectives. Founded by Bolanle Austen-Peters, LITF celebrates theatre

item.title: Her Enterprise, Africa’s Advantage: HerSphere Global Summit 2026 Convenes Africa’s Foremost Women Leaders in Lagos
item.description: Africa’s economic story is increasingly being written by women. Across the continent, women own and operate a remarkable share of small and growing enterprises, sustain household and community economies, and drive innovation in sectors from finance and technology to the creative industries. Yet the gap between participation and power remains wide. Too many women-led businesses stay small, under-capitalised and absent from the rooms where markets, policy and capital are shaped. On Tuesday, 17 November 2026, the HerSphere Global Summit 2026 will gather a distinguished assembly of leaders at the Wole Soyinka Centre, Lagos, Nigeria, to confront that gap directly. Proceedings begin promptly at 9:00 a.m. A Theme That Demands Action This year’s theme, “ Her Enterprise, Africa Advantage: Moving Women-Led Businesses Beyond Participation to Economic Power,” reflects a deliberate shift in the conversation. The question is no longer whether women belong in Africa’s economy — that has long been settled. The question is how women-led enterprises can scale, command capital, influence policy and build institutions that endure. The summit is designed to move beyond inspiration to strategy: how women founders access growth finance, how they enter regional and global value chains, how public institutions and private capital can work together to back them, and how today’s enterprises become tomorrow’s market leaders. An Exceptional Line-Up of Voices HerSphere Global Summit 2026 brings together an exceptional roster of women who have shaped Nigeria’s and Africa’s judicial, public, financial, entrepreneurial and creative landscapes: • Hon. Justice Amina Adamu Augie (CFR) • Dolapo Osinbajo • Hannatu Musa Musawa • Godrey Ogbechie • Maisie Dunbar • Bolanle Austen-Peters • Uche Pedro • Jumoke Olaniyan • Monisola Olufunke Alabi • Brenda Nwagwu • Chioma Ude • Adesuwa Okunbo Rhodes • Ifeoma Uddoh • Temilade Aduroja • Lehle Balde • Arese Ugwu Together, they represent decades of leadership across law, public service, investment, media, entertainment, financial inclusion and enterprise building — and a shared conviction that Africa’s prosperity depends on the full economic power of its women. Backed by Institutions That Shape the Economy The summit is supported by a strong coalition of partners: the Lagos State Government, the Office of Sustainable Development Goals (Lagos Global), the Nigerian Exchange Group (NGX), Delphino Entertainment, and SheMeansBusiness by BusinessDay. Their involvement underscores a growing recognition across government, capital markets and media that empowering women-led enterprise is not a social side-project — it is core economic strategy. item.title: 'Now everything changes': SpaceX catches Starship upper stage for 1st time ever (video)
item.description: null SpaceX caught the upper stage of its Starship megarocket for the first time ever today (Nov. 14), a landmark achievement that could unlock the giant vehicle's immense potential. Starship launched on its 15th test flight on Friday evening (Nov. 13), rising into the sky from SpaceX's Starbase site in South Texas. The mission plan called for bringing both of the vehicle's stages back to Starbase and catching them with the launch tower's "chopstick" arms — an unprecedented total recovery of an orbital rocket . That didn't happen; Starship's Super Heavy booster diverted to a Gulf of Mexico splashdown on Friday after experiencing a low-fuel alarm. But Ship succeeded in its attempt, notching a huge milestone for SpaceX and its dream of full rocket reuse. "That was the missing link," SpaceX's Dan Huot said during the company's landing webcast today, his voice thick with emotion. "That was the holy grail of spaceflight, plummeting through fire to be snatched out of the air by steel. We caught a Starship, and now everything changes." SpaceX caught the upper stage of its Starship megarocket for the first time ever today (Nov. 14), a landmark achievement that could unlock the giant vehicle's immense potential. (Image credit: Josh Dinner/Space.com) The Ship catch occurred today at 4:20 p.m. EST (2120 GMT; 3:20 p.m. local Texas time), roughly 22.5 hours after Flight 15 lifted off. Many SpaceX employees went outside to watch the vehicle, known as Ship 42, descend through the clouds toward its Starbase launch tower, which the company calls "Mechazilla." And they got quite a show: Ship 42 nestled gently into Mechazilla's waiting arms, while "Baby Come Back" played over SpaceX's landing webcast. "This is so incredible to see," SpaceX's Jessie Anderson said during the livestream. "One of the most incredible and historic engineering feats of all time has just happened right in front of our eyes." Why was this such a big deal? SpaceX had already caught Super Heavy — on three previous Starship test flights, in fact. But it had never tried before with Ship. The upper stage is a tougher target, for it flies higher, farther and faster than the booster. Indeed, on Flight 15, Ship 42 came all the way back down from orbit. Ship 42 comes in for its landing on Nov. 14, 2026. (Image credit: SpaceX) While the double-catch attempt, and the chopsticks success with Ship, were Flight 15's main headlines, the mission had other objectives as well. One was getting Ship to orbit, which had happened on just one previous Starship launch — Flight 14 , which lifted off on Sept. 28. Ship deployed 26 of SpaceX's next-gen Starlink V3 broadband satellites in low Earth orbit (LEO) on Flight 14, and it did so again on Flight 15. These 52 spacecraft are the first members of a constellation that will eventually consist of 100,000 satellites , if all goes according to SpaceX's plan. item.title: James Webb telescope finds ice older than the star it orbits
item.description: Beta Pictoris is a young star, roughly 20 million years old, and located about 64 light-years away from Earth. It is surrounded by a vast disk of dust and rubble where planets are still forming—astronomers have already found three. In a new Science study, a team led by Sarah Betti, an astronomer at the Space Telescope Science Institute in Baltimore, used the James Webb Space Telescope to look for ice in this disk. Researchers found both water and carbon dioxide ice. The water ice is glassy rather than crystalline, and it is mixed with carbon dioxide in roughly the same proportions we see in comets of our own Solar System. This suggests ingredients necessary to form water-rich worlds might be common around young stars. The missing ice Beta Pictoris is one of the best studied stars in the sky. Its disk was among the first ever imaged, back in 1984, and we see it almost exactly edge-on, which makes it a natural laboratory for studying how planetary systems grow. It's what astronomers call a debris disk, where the dust is constantly replenished by collisions among comets and planetesimals, small bodies that are the building blocks of planets. item.title: Winemakers are learning that conservation can be good for business
item.description: More than 500 vineyards are scattered across the slopes and valleys of South Africa’s Western Cape , one of the world’s most biologically diverse landscapes. The region produces about 90 percent of South Africa’s wine , but winemakers there are increasingly struggling with drought, excessive heat and erratic rainfall. Temperatures in the region have risen 1.5 to 2 times faster than the global average over the past five decades. And extreme storms have become more intense as climate variability increases. The late 2010s brought a significant challenge for winemakers, as three years of severe drought placed vineyards under intense stress and reduced grape production. As climate variability places increasing pressure on grape production, many wine producers are building on sustainability measures that have long been part of vineyard management. item.title: See Jupiter and Mars make a spectacular close approach overnight Nov. 15-16
item.description: null Heads up stargazers! Mars meets Jupiter for a spectacular rendezvous in the heart of the constellation Leo on the night of Nov. 15-16, and they won't be this close again until July 2029. Jupiter and Mars will appear a little over 1 degree from each other as they rise over the eastern horizon around midnight for viewers in the U.S., as the blue-white light of the main-sequence star Regulus glows below, according to In-The-Sky . It's all a trick of perspective, but spectacular nonetheless. In reality Mars and Jupiter are separated by a gulf of over 368 million miles (592 million kilometers), while the light from Regulus has travelled for some 79 light-years before reaching Earth . The spectacular display occurs just once every 2-2.5 years , when Mars catches up to Jupiter as it plies its more distant orbit, making the pair appear side by side from our Earthly vantage point — an event known to astronomers as an appulse. Jupiter, Mars and Regulus will appear close together on the night of Nov. 15-16. (Image credit: Created by Anthony Wood in Canva.) Both Mars and Jupiter are "superior planets" whose orbits exist beyond that of Earth. As a result their disks always appear full to us through the eyepiece of a telescope, unlike the inner planets Mercury and Venus , which exhibit moon-like phases as they circle the sun . A 6-inch telescope can reveal the wildly differing natures of the solar system worlds. Slew your scope to Jupiter to spot the gargantuan cloud bands (and zones) that ring the gas giant , formed from masses of ammonia and water that travel in different directions through Jupiter's hydrogen and helium atmosphere, driven by powerful jet streams. How to measure distances in the night sky using your outstretched hand. (Image credit: Created in Canva Pro) Mars, meanwhile, appears as a reddish, ochre disk complete with dark surface features, where basaltic rock has been scoured clean of the iron-rich dust that covers much of its surface, according to NASA . Interested in seeing and capturing the planets for yourself? Then be sure to read our guide on everything you need to observe and photograph the planets of the solar system, along with our picks of the top telescopes , cameras and lenses for exploring the night sky in 2026. Editor's Note: If you would like to share your photos of Mars and Jupiter with Space.com's readers, then please send your photo(s), comments, and your name and location to spacephotos@space.com.

item.title: Microsoft's school email bill gives rivals something to smile about
item.description: The fallout from Microsoft's education price rises and service cuts continues as institutions weigh the prospect of bigger bills, and the Windows maker's rivals struggle not to pull "I told you so" faces. The main takeaways are that free student email and collaboration services are being retired, and storage entitlements are changing. These changes generally apply at institutions' first renewal or extension on or after January 1, 2028. Microsoft announced the new plans last week, and the UK's Department for Education described itself as "disappointed" at the news. As well it might be, although the UK government has rarely seen a deal from Microsoft that it didn't like . Or, for that matter, other US tech giants . Exactly how much educational institutions will have to spend remains unclear. Mary Jo Foley of Directions on Microsoft put indicative student pricing at $2 per year for Microsoft 365 Education A2, $4 for A3, and $6 for A5, with Teams adding another dollar annually. Faculty licenses cost considerably more, while the new A7 student tier jumps to $385 a year before Teams. Foley cautioned that these were approximate figures, with actual prices set by Microsoft's partners. The new no-cost student tier, Microsoft 365 Education A0, is a poor replacement for Office 365 A1: it excludes Exchange Online, SharePoint Online, and Teams. Eligibility also requires full paid faculty coverage on A2 or higher and students who actively use Windows devices for education – potentially awkward for institutions running fleets of Chromebooks. A few dollars per student might not sound alarming. Multiply that across an institution, however, and something that used to be free becomes a recurring bill. Michael Meeks, CEO of Collabora Productivity, told The Register: "Free was the bait on the hook, and Microsoft spent years reeling in schools' email accounts, documents, identity management and classrooms onto its cloud." A poster on the edugeek.net forums commented: "This was always going to happen, I remember thinking this when we moved over to the MS free cloud solution. It will be free until they decide it isn't." The risk for Microsoft is that there are options. Meeks told us: "Schools now have a year to plan, and, in our experience with other large-scale educational projects, such as the University of Lille, that can be enough time to migrate properly." Other options include Nextcloud, which will be rolled out as part of Germany's Educational Cloud Infrastructure . Several Swiss universities also migrated to the service over an August weekend. According to Nextcloud, 39,500 students, teachers, and researchers, along with 585 terabytes of data, were shifted. Both Nextcloud and Collabora Productivity also highlight another factor that could drive educational institutions away from Microsoft: sovereignty.
